`fingerpost` additionally records, per arm, that the sign's `facing` equals the direction the arm
was built along - `tests/test_wayfinding.py::test_every_arms_direction_matches_its_own_signs_facing`
pins it so a placard can never point one way while naming a destination in another.

### Where these should go - not wired into any config, by design

Nothing here touches `mcbuild/planner.py` or any zone's config; several sessions are already
editing that file. What follows is the sites this audit's own numbers point at.

**Every zone, at its hub crossing** (`park paths`'s own centre - frontier 97594/80400, midway
97594/80600, hollow 97594/80800): one `fingerpost`, 3-4 arms. Midway's should carry an arm toward
**MIDWAY CENTRAL**, not toward the Frontier/Hollow arches - the fingerpost is the honest signpost
the arches cannot be until the arch/corridor mismatch above is resolved.

**Just inside the Park Gate** (midway, west edge): one `noticeboard` (rules/hours) and one
`mapboard` (`zone: midway`) - the first two things a visitor should see, in that order, before
the first hub decision.

**At each transit station's platform**: a `marker` naming the station, reinforcing the
departure board `transit.py` already builds - useful from a distance the board is not read at.

**At both sides of the frontier and hollow jump** (X=97638 and X=97640, at z~80433 and z~80776):
a `marker` or the noticeboard's own "MIND THE GAP" idiom, until the seam itself is resolved.

**Beside Frontier Arch, Hollow Arch, Frontier Gate and Hollow Gate**: a `fingerpost` or `marker`
redirecting to the real transit station - the one piece of signage that is not optional, because
without it these four thresholds actively mislead rather than merely doing nothing.

**One `archway` per zone**, at the point each zone's own plaza floor meets the transit corridor
(roughly X=97636-97638, at the zone's own hub Z) - "ENTERING THE SKYWAY," the one place in the
whole audit where two different designs' floors actually meet and a visitor needs telling they
have crossed from one to the other.

### What this pass did not do, stated rather than hidden

- **Nothing is placed in any config.** `emit`/`plan --approve` never ran on this; the sites above
  are coordinates and counts for wiring in, not a shipped design.
- **The flood model is a heuristic, not the mod's real `Nav`.** It has no corner-cutting rule, no
  fluid check, no `standoff`/`escape` logic - it is deliberately the simplest model that could
  answer "does a floor connect these two points," calibrated against the fact this project has
  learned twice already: vine and grass are not footing, and a chunk with nothing in it is not
  evidence of a hole. `Y_BAND` and the gap-1 rule are stated in `tools/park_flow.py`'s own
  docstring rather than assumed.
- **`known_destinations()` depends on `configs/park_line.yaml` existing on disk** for the station
  names half of its roster; it degrades to an empty set rather than crashing if that file is
  missing, and `tests/test_wayfinding.py::test_a_transit_station_name_is_accepted_as_a_destination`
  skips (not fails) when it is.
- **2,667 Python tests, 0 failures, 12 skipped** (`python -m pytest -q`), the 12 pre-dating this
  session. `tests/test_wayfinding.py` is 238 of the 2,667: every kind at every land and facing,
  connectivity, legality, economy, sign support, the roster, and the arm/sign-facing agreement.

## The park becomes a place: purpose, packing, and the bugs that were silent (2026-09-01)

Jack looked at the shipped park and gave the verdict the pipeline could not: *"im unclear what the
centyer monument fountain thing is or what purpose it serves"*, *"we dont need a bakery or that
building"*, *"the water rides are mostly not functional or leak water"*, *"park_right ... serves low
function and feels confusing"*, and the line that governs the rest - **"we don't want empty
structures that sit there and are mostly useless"**.

The park went from 81,000 blocks of buildings to ~126,000 blocks of buildings, games, a show, a
railway and a causeway. The more useful half of the session is the defects found on the way, every
one of which passed every check this repo had.

### THE THINGS THAT DID NOTHING, QUIETLY

- **`circuits.pulse` WAS A REPEATER, AND A REPEATER DOES NOT PULSE.** It delays both edges, so a
  held input gave a held output: a lever left on drove the output high for **21 of 24 ticks**
  against a contract promising two. Every casino game runs its button through it, so the house
  paid for as long as a player leaned on the button. It survived because its own test asserted
  `high < 20` out of twenty - **a bound looser than the bug**, which a permanent delay satisfies
  as easily as a pulse. It is a comparator-subtract monostable now.
- **THE MONUMENT'S RISERS SAT ON EVERY TREAD.** The cell tying each spiral step to the last was
  placed one course ABOVE the previous tread - the cell a player standing there occupies. All 39
  steps were unwalkable. Legality, economy, connectivity, the tread-path check and the
  stair-facing check all passed, **because every one asks about BLOCKS and the failure was in the
  air.** Assert headroom, not just treads.
- **A POST RESTING ON A RAIL DRAWS EXACTLY LIKE A POST RESTING ON THE GROUND.** The teacups' six
  canopy posts sat at a radius that put four of them on the loop's own rectangle; the loop is laid
  afterwards, so it overwrote each post's ground cell with rail and left the post in the course
  above. The Ghost Train had it worse - a solid block over **eleven of fifty** track cells, which
  is a suffocation tunnel - and shipped with **zero light sources**, because both lamp calls
  returned False into a variable nobody read.
- **THE LOG FLUME DRAINED 199,959 CELLS TO Y-1908.** The generator self-checked with
  `fluids.carries`, which asks whether the ride PATH is wet and moving. Whether every water cell
  is ENCLOSED is a different question and nothing asked it. `fluids.escapes` and
  `fluids.unenclosed` exist now - and the "count the open faces" audit that preceded them was too
  weak by four orders of magnitude.
- **THE PLAZA'S OBSTACLE LIST SILENCED IT COMPLETELY.** Handed the fifteen buildings standing in
  it, `_plaza` found no legal slot for a bed, a tree, a terrace or a pool, planted NOTHING, and
  reported `trees: 0, beds: 0` while shipping 6,405 cells of bare paving. **A guard strict enough
  to produce silence is indistinguishable from a feature nobody wrote.**
- **`circuits.randomiser` READ `dy` WHERE IT MEANT `dz`** - broken at north and south facings,
  which the casino's own Colour Wheel uses.
- **`_paste` COPIED BLOCK STATES AND NOT SIGN TEXT.** A sign is two things in two halves of a
  litematic; the pasted archways would have shipped blank.
- **A SHOOTING GALLERY WITH ELEVEN TARGET BLOCKS AND ZERO REDSTONE.** A `target` emits a signal
  proportional to accuracy and nothing read it.

### THE PACKER WAS LYING ABOUT CAPACITY, FIVE WAYS

The midway reported NO SITE for its carousel, its swings AND its teacups - every ride in a
fairground - **with the plot 43% used**. Five independent causes:

- **The Big Wheel was parked mid-plot**, casting a 19x77 strip that split the zone into three bands
  none of which was 33 wide. A landmark belongs on an edge.
- **The fine scan started three cells in from the boundary.** A monument pinned to the plot centre
  leaves exactly two 33-deep bands, so every candidate overhung it. Three cells of politeness cost
  three rides.
- **The scan stepped by two, and a stride has a PARITY.** The free band began on an even cell and
  the scan tried only odd ones. **The third time in this file a stride has hidden the answer it
  was searching for.**
- **SPACING WAS COUNTED TWICE** - every reserved box carried it and every candidate added it again,
  so buildings sat four cells apart where two was asked.
- **Candidates were sorted by distance from the CENTRE**, so everything packed inward and the
  leftover was a ring - wide, thin, never square. Sorting by CONTACT with what is already there
  keeps the free space in one piece, and is also what a street looks like.

### A FOOTPRINT IS NOT THE SAME AT EVERY FACING

Siting reserves a square so a turn decided afterwards is safe - which assumes a turn swaps width
for depth and nothing else. The Fortune Wheel's booth grew a roof on one side: 21 wide facing east,
23 facing west. It turned two cells into a dead tree with every check upstream correct. Three
reservation rules were tried and each fixed one zone and broke another. **The fix that worked is
local: the turn TRIES ITSELF and declines when the result collides**, which no future generator can
break. A building keeping its back to the street is a smaller fault than one built through its
neighbour.

### A RESERVED STRIP HAS TO SHRINK EVERYTHING THAT READS THE PLOT

The transit corridor is ten columns down the east of every park plot. Seeding it into `taken` stops
the PACKER and nothing else. Four more fixes:

    the edge branch     slid along an edge it did not own   (Big Wheel and Clock Tower on the rails)
    the cover branch    centred an 88-wide plaza across it  (claims nothing, so nothing objected)
    the streets         clamped avenues to the PLOT         (every zone reached X 97646)
    street furniture    checked `plot.contains`             (a bench on the railway)
    the turn pass       re-placed a sited module into it    (the Mine Head, two cells over)

`_owned_bounds` is the one source now. And **`width` is the FRONTAGE, which on an east-facing
module is Z** - written 88x96 the plaza came out 96 across X, paved ten columns of railway, and
left the carousel on bare void because Z was three short.

### The flow audit, and the gateways that led nowhere

Flooded over the SHIPPED litematics rather than the planned routes: strict floor-only walking
reaches **31%** of standable surface; allowing one jumpable gap reaches **80%** and all 36
attraction doors. The cause was a one-block unmarked gap at X 97639 where two of three zones fail
to meet the transit pad. The furthest attraction is **~436 walking blocks** from the gate.

And the finding that mattered most: **Frontier Arch, Hollow Arch, Frontier Gate and Hollow Gate all
led to nothing at all.** They sit on the north and south plot edges; the railway runs down the east.
`transit.py`'s own docstring had said so and nobody drew the conclusion. The geometry was right -
all four sit on X 97591..97599 facing each other across the gaps - and what was missing was LAND.
`gen/isthmus.py` is that land: a shell rather than a slab, flared at each plot and pinched to a neck
at the midpoint, 41,079 blocks with a sculpture trail, and a flood fill proves the walk end to end.
**Its shape was seeded from Python's `hash()`, which is salted per process** - every rebuild would
have produced a different, untested causeway.

### What replaced what

The rule applied throughout: **a structure that answers "what can a player DO here?" with "look at
it" is either given a function or replaced.**

| out | in | because |
|---|---|---|
| Guest Services | Hall of Fame | an information counter is a fitting nobody can use |
| The Arcade (a pavilion), Hoopla | plinko, high striker, prize counter | the old games were watch-a-randomiser; these take a PLAYER INPUT |
| The Riverboat | Gold Sluice | a hull you walk onto, against a launder you drop items into that rings a bell |
| Shooting Gallery | Shooting Range | eleven targets nothing read, against one that scores by accuracy |
| The Graveyard, The Chapel | Ghost Train and The Plummet fit | the hollow had two things to look at and needed two things to ride |
| the bakery | two shops with real interiors | `_deal` hands out `options[0], options[1]` before shuffling, so the head of the table IS the two-shop street |

**The eight arcade machines are the first games here where what the player does decides the
outcome.** `target` gives an analog signal by accuracy; an `item_frame` is an eight-position dial a
comparator reads; a `lectern` reports its page; a weighted plate is a scale; a `sculk_sensor` hears
you. None of that vocabulary had been used before.

## The causeway sculptures, replaced - and the pass that was eating them (2026-09-01)

Jack, on the shipped isthmus: *"ladybug sucks and is all glowing etc, we need a new sculpture
there, similarly i think we dont need 2 standing birds, lets replace flamingo with something
else that works really nicely and will fit"*. Two complaints, two unrelated causes, and the
first of them was not the ladybird's fault at all.

### THE GLOW WAS `_delight`, AND IT WAS TURNING THE SCULPTURES INTO LAMPS

Measured on the shipped design before anything was changed: **1,138 `ochre_froglight` cells
placed by the night sweep, and every single one of them inside a creature's coat.** Not one
landed on terrain.

    black_wool 299 . red_wool 295 . lime_wool 147 . pink_wool 129 . stone 82 .
    light_gray_wool 71 . white_wool 35 . green_wool 25 . dark_oak_planks 16 . yellow_wool 11

That is the ladybird's shell, its spots and its leaf; the flamingo's body; the heron's neck.
1,352 froglights in a 41,079-block design - **3.3% of the whole causeway was a lamp** - and the
ladybird, being a broad convex dome with a big flat leaf under it, caught more of them than
anything else. "All glowing" is a precise description.

`isthmus._delight` patched every dark spawnable cell by replacing the block UNDER it with a
froglight. For terrain that is exactly right and is this island's own idiom. For a sculpture it
is vandalism, and the docstring cited `frog.py`'s *"in the skin, not on it"* for it - **a rule
about a HANDFUL of lamps a designer chose and placed, not a licence to perforate a coat
wholesale.** The rule that governs is `Island Night`'s, and this file simply had no cost model
to state it with: *a fixture ON a sculpture damages it - ordinary ground is cheap, a coat is
dear.*

The fix is that a sculpture's cells are RECORDED as it is pasted and handed to the sweep:

- a dark cell over **ordinary ground** still gets the flush froglight, unchanged;
- a dark cell over a **coat** gets `glow_lichen` in the AIR above it - `Lowland Glow`'s own
  answer, arrived at for exactly this problem on exactly this kind of surface (it is what lit
  the axolotl's back). It emits 7, it is passable, cheap and 1.19, and it **adds** to the
  sculpture instead of eating it: not one creature cell is replaced;
- and because 7 carries six blocks through air, the lichen is thinned to a 5-block separation
  and the model re-propagated, so a handful settles a whole flank.

**1,352 froglights -> 253. Fifty-six lichen. `delight_in_coat` is 0 and asserted, and
`spawnable_dark` is still 0.** The count is cross-checked without the bookkeeping as well:
every block a creature generator emitted must still be standing in the finished causeway, so a
shortfall in any of its own palette is a coat cell something overwrote.

**And it exposed a second bug the moment the stops grew.** `exclude` was one radius doing two
jobs - keeping ambient drifts off a stop, and keeping ambient LAMPS off it. Sized to the new
structures it left **534 columns of moss unlit** at a stroke, which the sweep then filled one
lamp per cell. *"A stop lights itself"* is only ever true of the stop's own FOOTPRINT, never of
twenty blocks of open shoulder around it; they are two radii now.

### FOUR SCULPTURES, FOUR SHAPES, AND NOT ONE GENERATOR USED TWICE

The old lineup was a heron and a flamingo - one generator and one body plan, differing by
colour and two curves, which `heron.py`'s own docstring says outright - plus a ladybird on each
span. **Four pieces showing two shapes.** `test_the_two_spans_use_different_creatures` could
never catch it, because two spans can differ while each repeats a shape the other already used;
the new check is on the KIND, across the whole causeway.

Chosen on this file's own measured line, PLANAR/COLUMNAR against VOLUMETRIC, not on taste:

| span | t | | shape |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frontier Reach | 0.14 | **heron** (kept, scale 0.9) | an upright column |
| | 0.82 | **sloth** on a bough | a body slung UNDER a line |
| Hollow Reach | 0.26 | **bat** under a gantry (scale 0.7) | a horizontal membrane sheet |
| | 0.80 | **gecko** on a stele | a vertical plane |

**A creature is sited with the thing it stands on, hangs from or clings to**, and that is all
the new work: a stele of the land's own masonry for the gecko (its own docstring asks for a
cliff), a two-pier gantry for the bat, and two posts under the sloth's own branch - both are
hanging animals and a causeway has no ceiling anywhere. Not one line of any creature generator
was touched. `dragonfly.py` was tried and dropped again for the recorded reason: its trapdoor
wings are five components by construction at any scale, and bridging them would be editing a
tested generator's silhouette to suit this file. `turtle.py`, `frog.py` and `axolotl.py` are
out because all three take a world CAPTURE and probe a ground band that assumes the lowland's.

### Three faults inside the siting, each of which shipped a clean audit

- **EVERY PASTED CREATURE NEEDS A QUARTER TURN AND TWO OF THEM DID NOT GET ONE.** `_paste` only
  offsets, so a generator keeps its long axis on world X - and a creature stop is itself offset
  along world X, which is the axis a walker on the spine looks straight down. A 39-block
  wingspan and a 28-block bough both shipped **EDGE-ON from the only place anybody stands**: a
  post and a lump. Invisible in a plan view and obvious the first time `tools/look.py` was
  pointed at the bearing the walkway actually gives you. The gecko had been turned by hand for
  exactly this and the rule was not generalised. `_turn` re-aims an `axis`, carries a vertical
  property through and REFUSES anything naming a horizontal direction - our renderer draws a
  wrong facing and a right one identically, which is the stair convention's own failure.
- **A GANTRY SHIPPED WITH ONE LEG.** A span is 101 rows and a stele is 33 of them; at t=0.86
  the far end lands PAST the plot the causeway stops against, `cols` has no column out there,
  and `_ground_pier` therefore built precisely nothing - no error, no missing-cell report, and
  the design still audits as ONE PIECE because the lintel carries it across. `_CREATURE_ZHALF`
  states each structure's own reach, the centre is clamped into the span and the clamp is
  recorded, and a test asserts no shipped stop ever needs the clamp.
- **THE GANTRY'S LAMPS WERE NEVER PLACED.** The beam's band went in first and the lamp loop was
  guarded by `w.has`, which was then true at every one of those cells - seventy dark spawnable
  cells fifteen blocks over the walkway, silently. The froglights ARE part of the beam's own far
  course now, not something laid on it afterwards. `transit._lamps`'s rule, in a new body.

And one thing only a render decides: **a hanging creature wants a marker stone, not a
pedestal.** Given the heron's own five-block plinth, the bat and the sloth each stood over a
two-course disc of the land's trim with nothing on it, and an empty plinth reads as a statue
somebody has taken away. Three blocks, enough to carry the name plaque.

### The rendered verdicts, recorded (2026-09-01)

`tools/look.py --sheet panel`, cut out of the FINISHED causeway so each is judged with its own
plinth, ground and lighting, at the bearing the walkway actually gives you.

**GECKO ON A STELE - PASSES, and it is the best thing on the causeway.** Head-on it is
unmistakable: head down, four limbs splayed with fanned toes, big orange eyes with black
pupils, the tail curling up and over, all on a black slab with a lit coping and two banded
courses. The value panel is a flat dark ground with a bright figure on it, which is what a
relief IS. Two honest limits: **you cannot name it from the silhouette, because the silhouette
is the wall** - that question does not apply to a figure read against a plane - and it is a
smudge by 6x. It is also the one stop with no glow problem at all, and by construction: a
sculpture on a vertical face has almost no upward-facing surface for a mob to stand on, so
there is next to nothing for the night pass to want to light.

**Its back is a blank 33x34 wall and that is left as it is, deliberately.** The stele's face is
turned toward the spine, so a walker on the walkway only ever sees the lizard; the blank side
is what you get looking at the stop from the far shoulder, which is a place nobody goes. It
carries the same banded courses as the front and it is not worth another two thousand blocks
of relief to dress a face with no audience - the deck gallery's own lesson, that a block placed
to move a number is a block placed for the wrong reason.

**HERON - PASSES, unchanged, and it is the control.** Stilt legs, S-neck, dagger bill, layered
wing; still reads at 3x. Kept for that reason and no other.

**BAT UNDER A GANTRY - PASSES close and at 3x, MARGINAL beyond it.** A gantry with a wide dark
membrane slung beneath it, two bone claws gripping the beam, the body and legs hanging below.
`spread` 0.75 beats 1.0 and that was measured, not assumed: fully spread the wing is one flat
plate, half-furled it keeps a stepped outline and the finger struts and black tips are the
tell. **Scale 0.7 is the largest that is still one piece** - 0.6 sheds two wisps, 0.8 and 0.9
shed three or four, 1.0 is whole again but 56 blocks wide, which forces a `t` between 0.30 and
0.70 and collides with the pool, the garden and the overlook. From fifty blocks it is a frame
with a dark mass in it.

**SLOTH ON A BOUGH - PASSES close, MARGINAL at 3x.** Close it is instant: a hammock body under
the branch, four limbs angling up to it, the pale mask and black eyes, moss on the back. It is
the smallest of the four (26 blocks) and it sits inside a timber frame, so at distance it is a
lump between two posts. Worth building bigger if it ever matters - `sloth.py` has no scale
parameter, so that is a change to the generator, not to the siting.

**Judge the palette in game.** Everything above is `render3d`, which draws every block as one
flat RGB out of the same database the palette picker optimises against - this file's oldest
recorded circularity. What these renders are ground truth about is GEOMETRY and OCCLUSION.

### The bill

**41,079 -> 43,151 blocks (+2,072, +5%), 0 problems, 0 expensive, 42,311 cheap and 840 ok.**

    ochre_froglight              1352 ->  253    -1099    the glow
    red_wool                     1606 ->    0    -1606    the two ladybirds
    pink_wool                    1090 ->    0    -1090    the flamingo
    polished_blackstone_bricks    126 -> 1999    +1873    the gecko's stele
    moss_block                  11854 -> 13416   +1562    the bigger stop bulges
    brown_wool                      0 ->  674     +674    the sloth and the bat
    glow_lichen                     0 ->   56      +56

## The causeway's two new sculptures (2026-09-01)

Jack, on the four stops the isthmus shipped with: *"get rid of the gecko and bat - those are
used assets, we want NEW things, identiy and buiild new scuiptures in those places"*. The heron
and the sloth stay. The hollow reach's two stops are now `gen/balloon.py` and `gen/wyrm.py`,
written for those two spots and for nothing else.

| | blocks | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| `THE AERONAUT` | 2,299 | a moored show balloon - envelope, four rope lines, a basket. t=0.26 |
| `THE PALE WYRM` | 985 | a hooded serpent reared off a black milestone. t=0.80 |

Both are all cheap tier bar 97 `deepslate_bricks`; both are one 6-connected piece at BOTH
orientations they can be sited at; neither places one block of light.

### The rule they were chosen against, and what it ruled out

CLAUDE.md's measured line is PLANAR/COLUMNAR against VOLUMETRIC, plus the third case the
download corpus added - **one convex mass carrying a pattern**, which is the ladybird and
`Warm Snooze`. A balloon is that third case with a column of rigging under it and nothing else
in it; a snake is the purest taper in nature and a hood is a flat plate. **Neither has a joint
anywhere**, which is the whole of what killed eight mammals here.

**A THEME PARK'S LANDMARKS DO NOT HAVE TO BE CREATURES, AND THIS REPO HAD NEVER TRIED ONE.**
The balloon is the first thing in `gen/` that is not an animal, a building or terrain, and it
is the easier of the two to name from a thumbnail by a wide margin.

Rejected, and why, so nobody re-derives it: an insect with planar wings (`dragonfly.py` is FIVE
components by construction and a new one would have the same trapdoor-gap problem); a moth or a
raven (too near the bat this replaces, and the heron); an armillary sphere or any ring form (a
voxel ring at this size is a jagged octagon, and it is diagonal-heavy exactly where
6-connectivity bites).

### THE WYRM'S FIRST BUILD WAS A COIL ROUND A COLUMN AND IT FAILED

Two and a quarter turns of banded body up a twenty-course obelisk. It was a real helix, one
connected piece, correctly tapered, correctly banded, and its **silhouette was a lumpy vertical
mass with a hook on the top** - a totem, or a chess piece. Nothing about it was nameable.

The cause is structural rather than tuning, and it is worth keeping because the idea will look
attractive again: **a coil round a column reads through COLOUR AND DEPTH, and its OUTLINE is a
bumpy column.** On this causeway there is nothing behind a sculpture but open sky, so the
outline is the whole of what survives, and every one of those 154 stations was being spent on
the one channel that does not carry.

Rebuilt: the coil is **one and a half turns at the BASE ONLY**, where it anchors the animal and
gives the plan a pair of concentric rings, and everything above it is spent on outline - a free
S of sixteen courses, a flared hood 11 wide and 9 tall with a dark rim and two eyespots, and a
head standing three blocks proud of the plate with an open jaw.
`test_the_coil_stays_at_the_BASE_and_the_rise_carries_the_outline` fails if that trade is ever
reversed.

Three smaller things came out of the same rebuild:

- **THE S SWINGS IN Z AS WELL AS IN X.** Kept in one plane the curve foreshortens into a
  straight vertical from the exact bearing a visitor standing on the spine has, and the animal
  reads as a post with a disc on it. A lateral weave costs nothing and keeps the profile's S.
- **THE HOOD'S RIM IS DARK BECAUSE A PALE PLATE AGAINST A PALE SKY HAS NO EDGE.** The rim is
  also what stops the plate reading as a paddle, and `black_wool` against `bone_block` is 175
  points of luminance - measured ACROSS families, which is the only place this economy's
  contrast has ever been.
- **THE MILESTONE MUST NOT BE BURIED.** The first coil started two courses up and swallowed the
  stone it was wound round, so the "pale animal on a black post" idea existed only in the
  docstring. The coil starts at 3.6 now and three banded courses show under it.

### Two faults that shipped clean and were caught only by looking

- **THE WYRM SHIPPED WITH ONE EYE. TWICE.** The eye was a computed offset onto a course where
  the skull is two cells wide, and the half-cell centring makes those two ASYMMETRIC about the
  midline - one side found a block, the other found air. No error, nothing in the audit,
  nothing in the component count, nothing in the bill. The probe now SEARCHES for a row wide
  enough to carry a pair and takes that row's outermost cells. **A feature that can silently
  half-exist has to be measured, not computed.**
- **A ONE-CELL SECOND COMPONENT.** The first tail was a thin dark tip laid over a thicker
  sweep, and the tip's last sphere came out at radius 0.62 detached - the ear-tip failure, in a
  build clean everywhere else. One path, one taper, banding chosen per station.

### The balloon: the gap is the feature, and eight gores was a beach ball

- **FOUR COURSES OF OPEN AIR** between the basket's rim and the envelope's mouth, crossed by
  nothing but four rope lines. Fill them and the silhouette is a blob on a stick. Same rule as
  the ladybird's spot spacing and the frog's hand: the negative space does as much work as the
  blocks, and `test_the_gap_under_the_envelope_is_REAL` asserts those courses hold exactly four
  cells.
- **THE RIGGING IS DEAD VERTICAL AND THAT DECIDED THE THROAT.** A real balloon's lines splay
  out to a much wider hem, and a splayed line is a DIAGONAL, which is not connected here. So
  the envelope pinches to a mouth no wider than the basket and the lines drop straight from its
  own corner columns. It is also what a balloon under inflation actually looks like.
- **EIGHT GORES IS FOUR FACES HEAD-ON, and it read as a beach ball.** A gore wants about four
  cells at the equator; a 16-wide dome has ~50 there, so ten gores is five cells. Ten it is.
- **THE CROWN VALVE IS ONE COURSE.** Given the top two it covered a disc of radius 5.5 out of
  7.5 and the PLAN - a view every visitor gets off the skyway - was a black hole with a
  red-and-white fringe round it. One course, and the gores are left to converge at the top the
  way a real envelope's do, which is exactly what a balloon looks like from above.
- **THE SCATTERED "WEATHERED PANELS" WERE DELETED.** They went in for tonal variety and read as
  dirty rectangles on clean fabric - the deck soffit's confetti in a third body. The tone comes
  from the gore, which is already a 158-point step; the one horizontal element is one band.

### The verdicts, recorded

**THE AERONAUT - PASSES both panels, at every bearing, and still reads at 6x.** It is the
strongest-reading thing on either span and the reason is not craft, it is category: a big
convex mass with a two-tone pattern is what this medium is best at, and everybody alive can
name a balloon. The value panel shows real rounding rather than a flat shape with a pattern on
it, and the plan shows gores converging - the money view a lot of sculpture here throws away.
*Minecraft player:* the basket, the sandbags and the rope gap are what make it read as a thing
somebody flies rather than a lollipop, and they are 77 blocks out of 2,299.

**THE PALE WYRM - PASSES at six of eight bearings, MARGINAL head-on and tail-on.** The
three-quarter views are the best: coil, weave, hood, head, in that order down the outline. The
profile silhouette is nameable on its own - a reared serpent. Head-on and tail-on the hood
dominates and it reads as a tall figure with a disc; the lateral weave stops that being a post
and does not fix it, and that is the price of a hood, which has to be square to *somebody*. At
6x it is a marker rather than a nameable animal - the balloon beats it there and always will,
because a taper is thin and a dome is not.

**Still open on it, and not guessed at:** it is 985 blocks against the balloon's 2,299 and it
shows at distance. Building it half again as big would fix the 6x reading and is a `scale`
away, but the stop's own room (`_CREATURE_ROOM` 13) has to grow with it and that widens the
causeway's bulge. Jack's call.

**Judge the palette in game.** Everything above is `render3d`, which draws every block as one
flat RGB out of the same database the palette picker optimises against - this file's oldest
recorded circularity. These renders are ground truth about GEOMETRY and OCCLUSION only.

### What the swap cost

**43,151 -> 39,903 blocks (-3,248, -8%), 0 problems, 0 expensive, 38,892 cheap and 1,011 ok**,
0 lamps in any coat, 0 spawnable cells dark.

    polished_blackstone_bricks   1999 ->  294    -1705    the gecko's stele, gone
    brown_wool                    674 ->  425     -249    the bat, gone
    moss_block                  13416 -> 11884   -1532    two much smaller stop bulges
    white_wool                      0 -> 1227    +1227    the balloon
    red_wool                        0 ->  942     +942    the balloon
    bone_block                      0 ->  572     +572    the wyrm

**IT GOT CHEAPER BECAUSE A SELF-CARRYING SCULPTURE NEEDS NO STRUCTURE.** A stele is 33 rows of
a 101-row span and a gantry is two piers and a 37-block lintel; a balloon's basket is five
cells across and a milestone is seven. That is the argument for writing a sculpture that brings
its own ground rather than borrowing one that has to be given some - `_site_standing` is three
lines where `_site_bat` is thirty, and there is no pier left that can miss its footing.

`_site_bat` and `_site_gecko` are KEPT and are no longer sited. A gantry and a stele are
general answers to "this creature hangs" and "this creature clings" and both are covered by
their own tests; deleting them narrows what the file can do without fixing anything. Putting
either back into `GAPS` is a decision about reusing an asset, not maintenance.


## The causeway's heron became a stegosaur (2026-09-07)

Jack: *"i think the heron should be switched to a dinosaure."* Then, on the first build:
***"i dont think this steogasur is acceptable, it feels bad, its asymmetric, theres issues."***
He was right on every count and the second half of this section is worth more than the first.

**THE HERON WAS A LEFTOVER AS WELL AS A PREFERENCE, AND NOTHING WOULD EVER HAVE REPORTED IT.** It
stood at the frontier end of the Frontier Reach under a plaque reading *"stands in the frontier
marsh"* - a land re-themed to the LOST PLATEAU weeks earlier, and a marsh that has never existed
anywhere on this causeway. Physically correct, legal, affordable, one piece, and describing a park
that is gone: the same class as the five Prismworks relays that outlived the modules they named.

**BOTH DINOSAURS THIS PARK ALREADY OWNS ARE IN SIGHT OF THAT PLINTH, so the answer was a new
generator rather than a paste.** Measured off their own sidecars rather than guessed:

| | |
|---|---|
| `PF Pterosaur` | x97604-97637 / z80406-**80449** - ONE BLOCK off the causeway's frontier end, fifteen from where the heron stood |
| `PF Sauropod` | x97681 / z80290-80370 - 117 blocks away, on the same rim walk |

Pasting either is exactly what retired the gecko and the bat from the hollow reach - *"those are
used assets, we want NEW things"* - so `gen/stegosaur.py` is the third bespoke piece written for
these two stops, beside `balloon.py` and `wyrm.py`.

**AND IT IS A STEGOSAUR BECAUSE THIS FILE'S OWN LIST SAYS SO.** The download corpus's amendment
names it directly - *"a stegosaur is a convex mass with planar plates (the ladybird category)"* -
and every part of it lands on the good side of PLANAR/COLUMNAR against VOLUMETRIC: one convex
arched mass, a row of one-block sheets, four columnar tapers, four more off the tail. No joint
anywhere has to be modelled. **1,508 blocks at length 34, one piece, seven materials, all cheap
tier, all 1.19, zero cells asymmetric in shape OR in colour.**

### THE FIRST BUILD WAS REJECTED, AND THE MEASUREMENT AGREED WITH HIM EXACTLY

Told it "feels bad, it's asymmetric", the useful move was to measure rather than guess - and
"asymmetric" turned out to be one number:

    left-right mismatches, block by block:  99 in SHAPE, 0 in COLOUR
    ...and all 99 were CREST cells

**THE CREST ALTERNATED, WHICH IS WHAT THE REAL ANIMAL DOES AND WHICH IS WRONG HERE.** A real
stegosaur is two metres wide and staggers its plates by a hand's breadth. A voxel one nine cells
wide has ONE CELL to say it with, and one cell does not read as a stagger, it reads as a mistake:
head-on the two rows are two chimneys at different depths, and in plan they are a drunk zigzag.
The generator's own docstring had argued the alternation was "6-connectivity and legibility
agreeing". It was 6-connectivity and legibility disagreeing, and only a render said so.

**THE ANSWER IS TWO ROWS PAIRED, NOT ONE ROW CENTRED AND NOT TWO ROWS STAGGERED**, and all three
were built before that was obvious. Centred on the sagittal plane every plate is its own mirror -
symmetric, and head-on the crest becomes a single one-block blade standing out of the spine, which
is a MAST. Paired at the same station either side of the midline is symmetric AND is what the
animal looks like from the front: two pale blades flanking a ridge with the spine between them. In
profile the pair superimposes into one plate, so nothing is lost in the view the walkway gives.

Two more faults came out of the same look, and both are recorded failures of this repo arriving
in a new body:

- **THE PLAN WAS A SLAB.** `_body` swept SPHERES, so a station's width in plan and its depth in
  profile were the same number by construction - there was no way to say "widest at the shoulder
  and the haunch" at all, and the plan came out as one constant-width mass from shoulder to rump.
  That is the jaguar's retirement verbatim. The spine carries a half-DEPTH and a half-WIDTH
  separately now and the body is lofted station by station: plan width runs 5-9-5-11-5, which is
  a spindle.
- **A LEG WAS BEING COUNTERSHADED AS IF IT WERE ITS OWN ANIMAL.** `_coat` measures each column
  between its own lowest and highest cell, which is right for a barrel and absurd for a leg: four
  courses got the full ladder, pale at the foot and dark at the top, so the animal stood on four
  grey posts and read as a barrel on a stone plinth. Everything below the body's own belly line at
  its station takes the flank tone and nothing else.

**AND THE PALETTE WAS THE "FEELS BAD".** Navy / teal / light blue with traffic-orange plates is
what a saturated primary reads as at this size: a toy. It is a desaturated earth body now with the
one thing on it that is not flesh being the one thing that is not an earth tone - `brown_wool` 79 /
`acacia_planks` 104 / `light_gray_wool` 141 under a `white_wool` 236 crest, which is 157 luminance
clear of the back it stands on and a bigger step than the orange ever gave. The skull and the tail
spikes are `bone_block`, so crest, skull and spikes read as one material family, which is what
they are in life. **And it turned out to unlock the surfacing pass as well** - `shell.slab_for`
refuses a `rotated_pillar`, so a log-coated animal can never be given half blocks, and wool,
planks and stone are uniform on every face. See "super blocky and rough" below.

### FIVE TRAPS, EVERY ONE ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN IN THIS FILE, EVERY ONE FALLEN INTO ANYWAY

- **`round()` IS BANKER'S ROUNDING AND THE FEET CAME OUT AS COMBS.** The legs stand at 0.150 of
  the length, which at length 30 is exactly 4.5 - and `round(4.5) == 4` while `round(5.5) == 6`,
  so every foot sphere skipped alternate columns. Four feet read as EIGHT ground patches, at that
  length and not at its neighbours. **The `_ball` docstring in the same file warns about this trap
  by name while the frame under it was doing it.** Rounding is half away from zero now (`_r`), not
  toward +inf: `floor(v + 0.5)` sends 2.5 to 3 and -2.5 to -2, a shape one cell wider on one
  flank, which is the squid's own mirror fault from a new direction.
- **A TAPER THAT ENDS UNDER ONE CELL CANNOT BE SWEPT INTO EXISTENCE.** The tail spikes detached at
  lengths 26 and 34 and **at neither of their neighbours, and not at the one being looked at**. A
  fine step is not a guarantee, it is a hope that scales; `_thread` lays a one-cell 6-connected
  core first, filling every corner ONE AXIS AT A TIME, and the sweep hangs on that.
- **THE PLATES STACKED ON THEMSELVES.** Probed live, the second course of a plate finds the FIRST
  course of that same plate as its own top and lands one higher again: every plate shipped as
  alternate courses with a hole between them, fifty four-cell strays, and only a component count
  could see it. The back is SNAPSHOTTED before any plate is laid. Same shape as the frog's
  `flank_v`: MEASURE THE MASS, NEVER THE ACCUMULATING BUFFER.
- **THE CREST'S SPACING HAD TO BECOME EXACT INTEGER GEOMETRY, AND TWO TRIES GOT IT WRONG.** Left
  to the width curve, `plate_half` scaled to 2.54 for the plate nearest the peak, `floor(2.54 +
  0.5)` is 3, and that ONE plate went from five cells across to SEVEN and fused with its
  neighbour - four plates read as three. Capping the width against `run / count` fixed that length
  and not the next, because the stations are floats and `_r` rounds them together about half the
  time. The WIDTH is chosen first and the PITCH derived from it as `2 * wi + 2`, which leaves
  exactly one cell of sky between neighbours at any length, count or curve; too many to fit and
  the plates get narrower and then fewer, never closer. **A crest that can merge under any tuning
  is a sail waiting to happen.**
- **THE ANIMAL SHIPPED WITH NO EYES AT LENGTH 24.** The nominal course was one cell above the
  widest part of a small skull, so neither side had anything to sit on; the wyrm shipped with ONE
  eye twice for the neighbouring reason. The probe walks DOWN from the crown for the first course
  carrying a solid cell at the same offset both sides, and RAISES if there is none.

And one instrument rather than a trap: **a refusal below the ground plane is not the same fault as
one off the end.** A foot pad is a sphere centred on the course the animal stands on, so its lower
half is always outside the box; a refusal in f or s is the sauropod's disaster - clipped to 22
blocks of 48 facing north, with a plausible small dinosaur still in the render. `refused` and
`clipped` are counted separately, and `clipped` is 0 at every facing and every length.

**A SCALE SWEEP IS THE ONLY THING THAT FINDS ANY OF THAT.** Lengths 22 to 54, all four facings:
one piece, two eyes, the crest exactly `2 x plates` separate pieces, zero clipped, and zero
asymmetry in shape and in colour. Four of the five traps above were invisible at the length being
looked at and visible two lengths either side of it.

### "Super blocky and rough" - and it was NOT the resolution (2026-09-07)

Jack, on the symmetric rebuild: *"it feels super blocky and rough, how do we make it smooth and
clean."* Four answers, and the order they were found in is the useful part: the two I expected to
be the fix were worth little, and the two that mattered were both bugs.

**THE OBVIOUS ANSWER WAS WRONG, AND MEASURING IT IS WHAT FOUND THE REAL ONE.** "Size sets a
ceiling; tuning sets the plateau" is this file's own rule, so the first move was to build the same
animal at length 44 and compare at the same framing. It is not smoother. It is slightly WORSE -
the lumps scale with it, so they arrive bigger rather than finer. **A defect that survives a 30%
increase in resolution is not a resolution problem**, and that single comparison redirected the
whole session.

#### The lumps were the LEGS, sticking out through the flank

The half-width at the shoulder and the hip was a number chosen by eye. Measured against what has
to fit inside it:

    hip:       stance 2.65 + thigh 2.38 = 5.03      flank half-width 3.67      1.36 PROUD
    shoulder:  stance 2.65 + thigh 1.77 = 4.42      flank half-width 3.57      0.85 PROUD

So every leg pushed a cell and a half out through the side of the animal and read as a lump stuck
on it - four lumps, at the four places a quadruped is supposed to be smoothest. Sized as
`stance + leg radius` the same cells become the HAUNCH and the SHOULDER, which is rule 1 of the
panel review said forward: *"legs must merge into the body as a haunch and a shoulder"*. The flank
goes continuous and the plan keeps its waist (5-9-7-11-5), because the widths are still bimodal -
they are just big enough now.

#### The "roughness" was mostly the COAT, and it was not geometry at all

`_coat` measured every cell's height as a fraction between ITS OWN COLUMN'S lowest and highest
cell. That is right for a barrel of constant section and absurd for a lofted body, where every
column is a different height: the band boundaries follow whatever each column happens to be, so
the three tones come out as **grey blotches wandering a course up and down across the flank**. A
close render reads it as mould on the animal. No amount of smoothing the mass touches it.

Measured against the belly and back lines the keyframes actually describe, the bands are
continuous by construction. Three rules came out of fixing it and all three generalise:

- **A LEG IS NOT ITS OWN ANIMAL.** Countershaded per column, a leg's four courses got the full
  ladder - pale at the foot, dark at the top - so it stood on four grey posts and read as a barrel
  on a stone plinth. Everything below the belly line is one tone.
- **COUNTERSHADING NEEDS THICKNESS.** Three bands want a section deep enough to hold three, and a
  tail two or three cells thick has room for none: every cell lands in a different band and the
  tail comes out as an alternating brown-grey chain, which reads as damage. Below five cells of
  depth a part is one tone.
- **AND THE DITHER MUST BE HASHED ON THE DISTANCE FROM THE MIDLINE.** Keyed on the column, the
  jitter is a different number on each flank, so the boundary wobbles independently either side
  and the animal came out **sixteen cells asymmetric IN COLOUR while its shape was exact** - the
  frog's own recorded fault, where each coat drift carried its own signed offset.

#### The two passes this repo already had, that this animal never ran

CLAUDE.md's ANIMALS section states the order as `mass -> relax -> features -> face -> coat` and
every quadruped here runs it. The stegosaur went straight from a lofted mass to its features.

- **`relax` is now step 2**, with both recorded guards: legs, neck and tail as `protect` (the rule
  that shaves a pimple off a shoulder eats a limb whole), and every air cell below the belly line
  as `forbid` EXCEPT the air inside a leg's own cylinder - because a dent in a leg is worth
  filling, and barring those would keep the legs as lumpy as they were. It is worth less here than
  on a smoothed loft: this mass measured **zero notches before and after**, which is the tell that
  it was never dented, only stepped.
- **`shell.slab_shell` halves every cell that sits proud of its neighbours**, and **`_chamfer`
  turns every one-course step into a ramp with a stair**. 99 shape blocks on a 1,570-block animal,
  which against the download corpus's 4.51 stairs per thousand cells is the first build in this
  repo to be in the right order of magnitude.

**AND THE HALF-BLOCK PASS REPORTED ZERO FOR AN HOUR WHILE LOOKING LIKE A PASS WITH NOTHING TO
DO.** A palette entry is an NBT Tag, and `str(Tag(10, {'Name': ...}))` is a repr - so every block
name read that way matched nothing, every colour lookup failed and `slab_shell` returned an empty
dict. `nbt.state_name` is the accessor and every test in this repo already uses it.

**IT WORKS HERE ONLY BECAUSE THE PALETTE CHANGED.** `shell.slab_for` refuses any `rotated_pillar`,
because the colour DB samples a block's TOP face and a log's top is end grain - matching
`acacia_log`'s orange top to `acacia_slab` once drew a bright orange line down a bear's back. Six
of this repo's eight quadrupeds are coated in LOGS and get no half blocks at all, and CLAUDE.md's
own note says the unlock is to build coats out of uniform-textured blocks instead. This animal's
coat became wool, planks and stone in the palette rebuild one complaint earlier, so the match is
not merely legal but close: `acacia_planks -> acacia_slab` at distance **0**, `stone -> stone_slab`
at **0**, `light_gray_wool -> andesite_slab` at 9, `brown_wool -> spruce_slab` at 15.

Every shape block actually placed is acacia or spruce - both witnessed in bulk on this server -
because `trusted_slabs` already makes rule 12's inference rather than trusting a table: Minecraft
ships a material family COMPLETE, so a server that has `acacia_planks` has `acacia_slab`.

#### What it measures

    body-skin spike_rate   28.7 -> 9.4      "a limb that seems to have gravel stuck to it"
    notches                0                no one-block dents anywhere
    shape blocks           0 -> 99          slabs 64, stairs 35
    left-right asymmetry   0 shape, 0 colour, comparing FULL states with the facing mirrored
    Isthmus                41,230 blocks, 0 problems, 0 leaks, 0 expensive

`tests/test_causeway_sculptures.py` gained `test_the_SURFACE_IS_SMOOTHED_and_not_merely_stacked`
(the three passes all fail SILENTLY - a build with every one switched off is legal, one piece,
correctly proportioned and audits clean) and `test_the_LEGS_do_not_stick_out_THROUGH_the_flank`,
which asserts the arithmetic rather than the picture. `_lr` compares full block states with the
facing mirrored now, not bare names: a stair facing the wrong way is a real defect and a bare-name
comparison cannot see it - the frog shipped 60 of 134 that way.

**Followed up the same day** - see `shell.stair_shell` below. The chamfer moved into `shell.py`,
grew an UNDERSIDE case, and went from 35 ramps to 106. What it turned out NOT to be is an
outer-corner problem: a stair ramps a cell's top or bottom, so a cell in the middle of a flank has
no face to treat and no stair can help it. What is left is the section changing in whole cells,
which is geometry rather than surfacing.

### `shell.stair_shell` - stairs, and the note that said they were impossible (2026-09-07)

Jack: *"attempt it, we should be always pushing the limits of our generators to make complex shapes
so we can make really clean and sophisticated representations."*

**IT IS IN `gen/shell.py`, NOT IN THE ANIMAL, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF DOING IT.** The module
already owned "which cells earn a slab" and its own docstring said the geometry was "ready for"
stairs; writing a second private copy inside one generator is how two rules for one question start
disagreeing. `stair_shell` is now available to the elephant, the giraffe, the frog and everything
after them, and `stair_for` derives its answer from `slab_for` rather than matching colour a second
time - so the two can never disagree about what a coat is nearest to, and the `rotated_pillar`
refusal that stops a log-coated animal getting partials at all is inherited rather than
re-implemented.

**BOTH REASONS `shell.py` GAVE FOR NOT DOING THIS WERE ALREADY FALSE, AND THE PARAGRAPH OUTLIVED
THEM BY WEEKS.** It said a stair is directional with no evidence to settle the convention from,
because *"the capture holds ten stair blocks and none of them records its state"*. CLAUDE.md
records the correction on its own page: the capture holds **463** stairs and their states are in
the palette NBT - the earlier reading looked at the bare NAME list, which drops properties. And it
said a mirrored stair would be invisible in our own renderer, which was true when it was written
and stopped being true the day `render3d.subdivide` went in for the frog's toes. **A stale
"cannot" is more expensive than a stale "should": nobody re-reads it, because it reads as settled.**

#### The rule, and where the cells actually are

    TOP    the top is open and EXACTLY ONE lateral neighbour is solid one course UP
           -> half=bottom, facing that neighbour
    UNDER  the bottom is open and exactly one lateral neighbour is solid one course DOWN
           -> half=top, facing that neighbour

Counted over the animal's own skin before anything was written, which is what decided the shape of
the pass:

    834  interior, walled both ways        no face to treat
    102  UNDER: flat underside
     87  TOP: plateau or proud             -> slab_shell's job, already done
     82  TOP: one higher                   -> a ramp, and only 35 were being placed
     67  UNDER: one lower                  -> A RAMP, AND NONE WERE BEING PLACED
     35  UNDER: two or more lower
     32  TOP: two higher, perpendicular    an inside corner: a stair there reads as damage

**THE UNDERSIDE WAS THE BIGGEST UNTAPPED CASE AND IT IS THE ONE THE CORPUS NAMES.** 27% of outside
builders' stairs are `half=top` - eaves, soffits, corbels, the underside of an overhang - against
none of ours. On an animal that is the belly line and the jaw, which together with the back line
is the whole of what a profile silhouette IS.

**AND `slab_shell`'s UNDERSIDE PASS IS OFF FOR A REASON THAT DOES NOT APPLY TO A STAIR.** A top
SLAB removes half a cell and reads as a gap wherever the thing being cut is thin - it once cut
visible slots through the elephant's ears. A `half=top` STAIR removes a QUARTER and leaves the full
depth on the side the mass continues, so it fills a corner rather than opening one. The thickness
guard is kept anyway and the ground course is never touched, or a foot hovers.

**A VERTICAL STEP IN A FLANK CANNOT BE CHAMFERED BY A STAIR AT ALL**, and that is worth knowing
before anyone tries: a stair ramps a cell's TOP or its BOTTOM, and a cell in the middle of a wall
has solid above and below. Measured, every stair this pass places faces along the body, because
those are the cells with an open face. The only tool for a vertical step is a vertical panel - an
open trapdoor, which is the corpus's other big finding and is architecture rather than anatomy.
What remains blocky on this animal is the flank's section changing in whole cells, and that is
geometry, not surfacing.

#### AND THE RENDERER DREW ALL 106 OF THEM AS CUBES

`render3d.render` does not subdivide - `tools/look.py` calls `r3.subdivide(m)` when
`r3.has_shapes(m)`, and the throwaway sheets I was judging from called `render` directly. So the
first look after adding the stairs was **identical to the look before adding them**, and the honest
conclusion from that picture would have been that the pass does nothing.

That is the frog's own trap, recorded on this page in capitals - *"the feet were rebuilt with
stairs and every sheet here drew them as full cubes, so the change was unjudgeable"* - fallen into
by the person who had just read it. **Judge shape work through `tools/look.py`, or subdivide by
hand; a scratch render script is not the renderer.**

#### What it measures

    shape blocks       99 -> 177 on 1,266 skin cells = 14%   (corpus median for detail: 17.3%)
                       stairs 106 (55 top, 51 under), slabs 71
    stair rate         0.64 per thousand cells across this repo -> 67 on this animal
    left-right         0 shape, 0 colour, comparing FULL states with the facing mirrored
    Isthmus            41,229 blocks, 0 problems, 0 leaks, 0 expensive

Every partial placed is acacia or spruce, both witnessed in bulk on this server, because
`trusted_slabs` already makes rule 12's inference rather than trusting a table: Minecraft ships a
material family COMPLETE, so a server that has `acacia_planks` has `acacia_slab`. `stair_for` then
checks the registry for the stair rather than carrying a hand-written map - `petrified_oak_slab`
and `smooth_stone_slab` have no stair, and remembering which do is rule 11's exact failure.

### Measured against the giraffe, which is the only way this got fixed (2026-09-07)

Jack: *"I feel like this is very rough and the face etc are less smooth than they should be, we
want this to feel like the giraffe."* **A reference beats an adjective**, and the first move was to
render the two side by side and put the repo's own roughness numbers on both:

                    spike_rate   notches   jerk_rel
    GIRAFFE               4.03         0        8.4
    stegosaur            28.97        10       20.5

That is not taste, and every one of the three names a defect you can see once you know to look:
`spike_rate` is "a limb that seems to have gravel stuck to it", a notch is a one-block dent "the
eye reads as damage", and `jerk` is the one that catches "it goes in and out".

#### THE PARAMETERS WERE THERE ALL ALONG AND I HAD UNDER-SET THEM

`quadruped.py` relaxes **four times at fill 11 and keep 11**. This ran ONCE at fill 15 and keep 8 -
weaker on every one of the three axes - because of an over-reading of this file's own warning that
*"every smoothing pass rewards thickening"*. **That warning is about tuning smoothing ALONE against
the rubric**, which took the bear's proportion 0.88 -> 0.50; it is not an argument for
under-smoothing, and the giraffe was standing in the world as the counter-example the whole time.
Swept against every contract at once, four rounds costs 21% more cells and keeps the plan waist,
the four feet, the eight crest pieces and exact symmetry.

**AND ONLY THE LEGS ARE PROTECTED, which is also what `quadruped.py` does.** A protected cell is
never shaved, so protecting the neck and the tail as well left them exactly as lumpy as they were
built while the barrel smoothed around them - the two parts that read worst against the giraffe. A
leg genuinely has too few neighbours to survive `keep`; a tail three cells thick does not.

    relaxed mass:   spike_rate 8.6 -> 3.92     BETTER than the giraffe's 4.03
                    notches 0, jerk_rel 20.5 -> 12.4

The finished model still measures 25 because the CREST is one-block sheets and scores that way by
construction; the giraffe has no such feature. The body skin is the fair comparison.

#### THE FACE WAS A BALL WITH A BEAD ON IT

Set beside the giraffe's head the gap is obvious: the giraffe has a pale muzzle narrowing to a
nose, an eye set in it, a jaw. This had a SPHERE of radius 2.4 with a black cube stuck on it.
**A skull is a TAPER** - a stegosaur's is long, low and narrow, ending in a toothless beak - and
none of that survives being drawn as a ball. Two more things had to follow:

- **THE NECK STOPS WHERE THE SKULL BEGINS.** Swept on to the nose it buried the head: only the
  last four pale cells showed past the russet, so the animal read as a neck with a chip on the end.
- **A NOSTRIL IS NOT BLACK, and it gets its OWN MATERIAL.** Black, two nostrils between two black
  pupils read as a second pair of eyes - the frog shipped exactly that. And drawn in the plates'
  own root stone, the crest mask counted each nostril as a one-cell PLATE with no back under it,
  so the plate-count, the plate-rooting and the "the nose is all bone" contracts all failed on a
  correct build. **A mark that means something different is a different block**, or every test that
  masks by material is measuring two things at once.

#### FIVE BUGS THE SCALE SWEEP FOUND, EVERY ONE SILENT AT LENGTH 34

Turning the smoothing up and un-protecting the neck and tail destabilised four things that had been
held together by under-smoothing. **Not one of them was visible at the length being looked at.**

- **THE LEG-GAP GUARD WAS TRUE FOR EVERY CELL ON THE MIDLINE.** `abs(sd) - stance < r` is negative
  at `sd = 0`, so the entire space between the legs counted as "inside a leg", was never forbidden,
  and the fill pass welded the feet - two instead of four at most lengths. It is
  `abs(abs(sd) - stance)`, the distance from the leg's own axis.
- **...AND THE REACH HAD TO BE CLAMPED TO HALF THE LEG SPACING**, which is this file's own sentence
  ("or it protects nothing"). At `r + 0.6` alone, a thigh 1.86 wide standing 2.34 off the midline
  reaches the midline anyway: three feet instead of four.
- **THE THAGOMIZER CAME AWAY AS ONE PIECE** at four lengths of seventeen. Un-protecting the tail is
  what smoothed it, and the same shave MOVES ITS SURFACE - the spikes still rooted at
  `_tail_y_at`, which is arithmetic. `loft.surface_out`'s rule, and it has already cost this
  project a mane, a pair of ossicones and a tail that floated 45 cells clear.
- **THE SKULL DETACHED AT LENGTHS 22 AND 26** for the same reason at the other end: the neck's thin
  tip is shaved by an amount that depends on the length, so a skull abutted to its DESIGNED tip
  ships headless. It threads back to whatever is actually there - and the THREAD reaches back while
  the SWEEP does not, because moving the sweep's own start stretches its taper and the cheek came
  out too narrow to carry a pair of eyes.
- **A PLATE'S OUTER WING CAME AWAY** at length 30 and not at 26 or 34. Each column roots on its own
  patch of back, and where the back drops two courses between one column and the next their ranges
  stop overlapping. Each column now reaches down to its lower neighbour's root.

**And the plate rows moved from one cell either side of the spine to two**, because at one the
trough between them measured as TWELVE NOTCHES - every notch in the animal - and the crest read as
a cracked ridge rather than as two rows. At two it is zero, which is what the giraffe measures.

#### Two tests were the wrong SHAPE, not the wrong number

- **"a plate meets the back at three or more cells"** failed the smallest plate of a correct build,
  whose root row is two columns wide where the back has narrowed. The exact property is that EVERY
  CELL OF A PLATE'S LOWEST COURSE sits on body - a threshold standing in for a property, which is
  what this repo keeps having to unlearn.
- **"the skin has zero notches"** cannot distinguish a crotch from damage. Four remain and all four
  are on the midline under the belly, in the gap the forbid set deliberately keeps open; the
  giraffe scores zero only because its legs are far apart and its belly is high. The assertion is
  now that every dent IS that gap, which is exact and still catches a dent anywhere else.

And `test_the_plates_are_PAIRED` reads the offset out of `_dims` instead of carrying the literal
`1`, or it would have failed the fix rather than the fault.

    Isthmus  41,461 blocks, 0 problems, 0 leaks, 0 expensive
    lengths 22..54, all four facings: one piece, 4 feet, 2 eyes, crest = 2 x plates, 0 clipped,
    0 asymmetric in shape and in colour

### The panel verdict, recorded (2026-09-07)

Cut out of the FINISHED causeway as well as alone, at the bearings the walkway actually gives.

**SILHOUETTE - PASSES, and it is the only question that finally matters.** With the colour taken
away it is an arched back carrying four separated plates, four columnar legs, a tail held clear of
the ground with spikes on it, and a small head low at the front. A stranger names it.

**PROFILE - PASSES, and it is the view the stop is built for.** The walk runs along Z and every
creature stop is offset in X, so a visitor stands ABREAST of this animal at about twenty blocks -
which is exactly the view a stegosaur's plates exist for. Both profiles are mirror images.

**PLAN - PASSES, and it is the second view rather than a spare one.** The skyway passes overhead,
and from there the two plate rows, the four splayed pads and the thagomizer all read. That is the
ladybird's own argument for this category: the plan is the view voxels give away free.

**HEAD-ON - MARGINAL, and honestly so.** Eleven cells wide, so head-on it is a narrow mass with two
pale blades over it. That is what a stegosaur looks like from the front and it is not a bearing
anybody is routed to here - but it is the weakest of the four and no arrangement of a paired crest
improves it further.

**At half distance it still reads. At a fifth it is a low dark mass with a bumpy pale crest** -
still a plated dinosaur and nothing else.

**The one real gap: there is not a single shape block in it.** The download corpus measures us at
0.64 stairs per thousand cells against their 4.51, and this animal is full cubes throughout. A
stair under each plate's outer wing and at the toes is the obvious next pass, and `render3d` can
now draw both - which is the argument for doing it rather than against.

### What it cost, and what is still open

    Isthmus  39,903 -> 41,171 blocks, 0 problems, 0 leaks, 0 expensive, 0 lamps in any coat
    the stop moved t 0.14 -> 0.24, because the animal reaches 22 rows back and 19 forward
             against a heron's 7, and at 0.14 its tail would have been CLAMPED - a clamped stop
             is one whose far end lands where `cols` has no column at all

`_site_heron` is `_site_footed` now and serves both; `SELF_CARRYING` in
`tests/test_causeway_sculptures.py` keeps the stegosaur out of the balloon's and the wyrm's
own-ground contract, because it stands on four feet on the causeway's plinth and its lowest course
is four separate pads.

**Two TESTS were wrong where the build was right, and both are worth keeping.**
`test_the_rim_carries_a_fence_wherever_the_ground_actually_ends` read the highest cell in a column
as its cap - and a sited creature is free to reach out over open air past its plinth, so a rim
column carries the ground, its fence, several courses of sky, then a bone spike hanging seven
above. Read that way the fence four courses below looked missing and **the causeway was reported
unfenced at the one place it is most obviously fenced**; the ground's cap is the top of the
column's own UNBROKEN RUN. And the plate-rooting test was written per COLUMN, where a kite's outer
wings legitimately overhang - it is per PLATE now. The right way round to discover a contract had
been written as "nothing overhangs" when what was meant was "nothing floats".

**Still open:** nothing here has been placed in game - `render3d` draws with the same colour DB the
palette picker optimises against, so judge form and mass off the sheets and the palette in world.
The night pass hangs **23 `glow_lichen` in the air over the animal** (`delight_in_coat` is 0, so
not one coat cell was eaten) and on a bone-white plate those read as green flecks rather than as
the patina they read as on a dark coat - correct by the causeway's own rule, and a causeway-wide
decision to change. And the seven pre-existing
`test_isthmus.py::test_every_land_pair_builds_legally[*-prismworks]` failures are still the stale
`wayfinding.known_destinations()` roster, unrelated and unfixed.


## THE STEGOSAUR IS RETIRED: FOUR POLISH ROUNDS CANNOT FIX A CATEGORY (2026-09-07)

Jack rejected it four times running, in four different words - *"it feels bad, its asymmetric,
theres issues"*, *"it feels super blocky and rough"*, *"very rough and the face etc are less smooth
then they should be, we want this to feel like the giraffe"*, and finally *"I think its an issue
still, it doesnt look good"* - and every round I answered with a better version of the same thing:
symmetry to zero, a plan spindle, legs that stop pushing through the flank, a skull that is a taper
rather than a ball, `spike_rate` 28.97 -> 3.92 (BETTER than the giraffe's 4.03), a whole new stair
surfacing pass in `shell.py`. Every one of those was a real improvement and it measured as one.
**None of them touched what was wrong.**

**IT IS A STANDING QUADRUPED, AND THIS FILE HAS SAID FOR WEEKS THAT THIS SYSTEM CANNOT BUILD ONE.**
The download corpus's own finding, recorded here under "Reading other people's builds": *the line
is not the species, it is whether the silhouette decomposes into LIMBS - a corpus of 31 outside
builds contains no realistically-proportioned quadruped at all.* Eight mammals were retired on that
evidence. I then read *"a stegosaur is a convex mass with planar plates (the ladybird category)"* -
which this file also says, in the Lost Plateau's re-theme - and sited one, and the two sentences
are about different halves of the same animal. **THE PLATES ARE THE LADYBIRD CATEGORY AND THE
ANIMAL UNDER THEM IS A JAGUAR**, and the plates are 12% of the cells.

The general lesson, and it is the expensive one:

> **WHEN FOUR ROUNDS OF POLISH EACH MEASURE BETTER AND STILL LOOK WRONG, THE FAULT IS THE
> CATEGORY, NOT THE EXECUTION.** A rejection that repeats in different words is evidence about
> the CHOICE; only a rejection that moves is evidence about the craft.

That is the same shape as this file's own note about the jaguar - *"the jaguar at 2.6x and 60,000
blocks failed exactly as the 27-block one did"* - and I had it in front of me each time and treated
the next round as a tuning problem. What broke the loop was not another render: it was stopping and
laying out the whole field of candidates, at which point the answer was obvious from the rule.

`gen/stegosaur.py` is kept, still builds, and keeps all of its tests. `taxonomy.live()`'s rule
applies to a bespoke sculpture exactly as it does to a species: **a retirement is a RECORD, not a
deletion** - it is out of `GAPS` and out of nothing else, because the eleven bugs its scale sweep
found are eleven bugs the next animal inherits the moment somebody copies its machinery.

### And the machinery came out into `loft.py` before it was copied

`Frame`, `r()`, `ball`, `sweep`, `thread` and `STEP` were all private to `stegosaur.py` and were
about to be pasted into a second file. Every one of them carries a bug this repo has already paid
for once - `r()` is half-away-from-zero because `round()` is banker's rounding and turned four feet
into eight combs; `thread` exists because a taper under one cell is a chain of DIAGONAL neighbours
and cost the pterosaur three spans and the stegosaur its spikes; `Frame.clipped` is counted apart
from `refused` because the sauropod shipped clipped to 22 blocks of 48 with nothing to say so. A
private second copy is a second place for all of those to come back.

## The Ankylosaur: the quadruped that does not decompose (2026-09-07)

`configs/isthmus.yaml` (the Frontier Reach's first stop), `mcbuild/gen/ankylosaur.py`.
**2,300 blocks, one piece, four feet, 0 clipped, 0 asymmetric, all cheap-or-ok.** Chosen off the
full candidate field rather than by taste: of thirteen dinosaurs, it is the one whose OWN ANATOMY
is the shape that survives here - a low armoured shield with the legs tucked under it, so the
silhouette never breaks into posts however it is lit or turned. It is not a stegosaur with better
smoothing; it is the animal that does not need the smoothing to rescue it.

Everything below found a defect that shipped a clean audit, a correct bill of materials, one
connected piece and a plausible render.

### THE PART COUNTS WERE `put()` CALLS, AND MAKING THEM CELLS FOUND TWO MISSING FEATURES

The squid's own recorded lesson - *"the sidecar reported 251,264 arm blocks in a 116,000-block
animal, which reads as a measurement"* - was applied here on the way past, and it paid for itself
inside a minute:

    spikes 1440 -> 118    head 1479 -> 114    HORNS 124 -> 0

**The horns placed 124 blocks and gained ZERO cells: they were entirely inside the skull.** Rooted
at a computed half-width rather than on the surface the relax pass actually left, they were the
frog's `forelegs: 0` exactly - a build with a part missing is still one piece with a clean audit -
and no call count could ever have shown it. `loft.surface_out`'s rule, which has now cost this
project a mane, a pair of ossicones, a tail that floated 45 cells clear and a pair of horns.

### FOUR MORE FEATURES THAT HALF-EXISTED, AND THE SWEEP IS WHY THEY ARE NOT SHIPPED

- **THE CLUB WAS A ONE-COURSE PADDLE BELOW LENGTH 34.** Its radii are fractions of the length, and
  a fraction goes under one cell long before the animal stops being buildable: at 26 the vertical
  radius is 0.73, `ball` fills a single course, and the club came out THINNER THAN THE TAIL
  CARRYING IT - at two lengths out of five, and not the one that was being looked at. Radii have a
  floor in BLOCKS now. It is `MIN_BLOCKS` said again: **a feature below its own legible size does
  not shrink gracefully, it stops existing.**
- **THE SKULL CAME TO A POINT.** The head is built as MASS, so the relax pass runs over it - and it
  fills a narrow trough and shaves a thin tip, so a deep pinch and a fine taper bought a defect at
  both ends: measured, the last five stations ran 7, 5, 5, 3, 1 and the animal had a SNOUT. An
  Ankylosaurus skull is famously wider than it is long. The taper stops short of the tip and a
  flattened wide ellipsoid caps it, which is what a beak is, and the pinch is shallow because a
  deep one is filled anyway. **Which primitive a part is, not what number it is set to.**
- **THE TAIL WAS A STUB, AND THEN A LOLLIPOP.** At 0.115 of the length past the rump the profile
  silhouette read as an armadillo; lengthened to a real 38% and left thin, it read as a THREAD
  WITH A LUMP ON IT. A club has to look carried, not hung, so the tail leaves the hip at nearly
  the rump's own girth.
- **AND THE KNOBS WERE POLKA DOTS.** In the PLAN - this animal's money view, and the one voxels
  give away free - a field of stark `bone_block` osteoderms on a brown back is a regular grid of
  white spots. The row-stagger test passed the entire time, because **staggered dots are still
  dots**. They are `dripstone_block` now, 33 of luminance over the back rather than 146: a raised
  bump catching light rather than a rivet. That leaves the bone to mean exactly one thing, which
  is the features that stand PAST the animal's outline - the fringe, the horns and the club. The
  frog's rule read backwards: *a mark that means something different is a different block*, so a
  mark that means the SAME thing must not be.

### Three test faults, and one of them deleted two tests silently

- **A MIRRORED PAIR OF ROWS IS NOT TWO ROWS.** The knob-lattice test keyed on the COLUMN, and this
  animal is exactly symmetric - so the row at +0.46 of the half-width and the row at -0.46 carry
  identical stations by construction, and every correct build failed for being a lattice. It is
  keyed on the distance from the spine.
- **A KNOB SITS ON THE BODY AND A SPIKE STANDS PAST IT.** Masked as "armour above the belly" the
  fringe came in too, and the fringe runs every station of the rim. The two are told apart by what
  is UNDER them, which is what they actually are.
- **TWO OF MY TEST NAMES COLLIDED WITH THE STEGOSAUR'S AND PYTHON SILENTLY SHADOWED THEM.** The
  count stayed at 65 while I added three tests, which is the only reason it was caught -
  `test_it_survives_EVERY_LENGTH_it_can_be_built_at` defined twice in one module is not an error,
  it is two deleted tests. **A suite's own collected count is evidence and should be read.**

### THE FACE WAS THE ONE THING NOTHING TESTED, AND IT SHIPPED AS A THUMB

Jack, on the finished animal: *"the face sucks."* It did, and the head had passed every geometric
contract this file had written for it - blunt, wide, a run of stations narrower than the shield,
carrying a pair of eyes, symmetric. **All of those are true of a smooth brown lump.** A face is a
DRAWN feature and nothing was asserting the drawing.

- **THE SURFACING PASS WAS RUNNING OVER THE MUZZLE.** `shell.py` chamfers a step by replacing the
  cell with a stair of the nearest colour, and on the head it picked a green-grey slab and an
  orange stair out of the coat's own colour families - so the face was a staircase in three tones
  nothing else on the animal uses. The frog states the rule for its own build - *only the skin,
  and only single steps; the face, the belly, the eyes and the feet are drawn features and a stair
  through one of them is a hole in a drawing* - and it belongs in `_skin` rather than in each
  caller, or the next pass added here forgets it.
- **THE EYES WERE ON THE SKULL ROOF.** Walking down from the crown for the first course carrying a
  pair puts the beads on TOP of the head, where no bearing but the plan can see them. An eye
  belongs on the skull's front corner - visible head-on at the silhouette's edge and in profile -
  and that is where a real one is.
- **AND THE HEAD HAD NO MOUTH.** The frog's own recorded finding is that five passes of eye work
  went into a front that was a pale rectangle and what fixed it was ONE DARK LINE across it.
  `_face` draws four marks: a pale keratin beak on the front cap, that line where the jaws meet
  and carried three stations back along each jaw, two nostrils, and the bead.

Five things it cost, in order:

- **A BEAK IS THE FRONT CAP, ONE CELL DEEP.** Painted as every cell of the front three stations it
  is not a beak, it is a grey HEAD - 84 cells, and the animal came out with a robot's face. It is
  FOUND (the frontmost solid cell of each line through the skull) rather than filled: 8 cells.
- **A MOUTH IS ONE COURSE.** Laid on the lowest cell of every beak column it read head-on as a
  black cavern under a grey mask.
- **A DRAWN FEATURE MUST NOT REPAINT ANOTHER ONE.** `Frame.put` records `fixed` and does not
  enforce it, so the beak pass would happily paint over an eye - and an eye that has been painted
  out is a build with a part missing that audits perfectly clean.
- **THE EYE MERGED WITH THE MOUTH.** The jaw line runs back along the cheek, and at 0.30 down from
  the crown the bead landed one course above it: two black cells touching are one black blob,
  which is the axolotl's *"a two-cell bar, not a bead"* and the frog's sunglasses arrived at from a
  third direction. Two courses of hide between them.
- **A NOSTRIL IS NOT BLACK AND IT IS NOT THE FACE'S OWN TONE EITHER.** Black, two of them under two
  black pupils read as a second pair of eyes - the frog shipped exactly that. Moved to the head's
  own `dripstone_block` they were invisible, and reported 2 while placing nothing anybody could
  find. They are the back's brown on the face's dripstone: 33 of luminance, a dimple.

**AND THE FACE MOVED THE ANIMAL'S SIZE FLOOR.** `_eyes` began raising at length 26: the relax pass
leaves a skull one course tall there, which cannot hold a bead either side of a midline. Two bugs
came out of chasing it - a pinned eye STATION (at 26 and 30 the skull is one cell wide at the
corner, so it must search back toward the cheek and take the frontmost station that carries a
pair), and a course range whose start fell BELOW its own floor, so `range(1, 1, -1)` was EMPTY and
**a loop that cannot execute looks exactly like a loop that found nothing.** With both fixed the
floor is a real one and the declared minimum is **28**, not 26: `tools/scale.py`'s doctrine is that
an animal's critical size is the largest of its features' own floors, and the face is now one of
the features.

`test_the_face_is_DRAWN_and_reads_head_on` and `test_the_SURFACING_pass_keeps_off_the_face` are
what stop it going back. Two of that first test's assertions were weaker than they looked and both
are worth keeping as a shape: **"the outermost black cells are the eyes"** picks the mouth's own
jaw line about as often, so a bead is defined as black with no black above or below it; and
**"the bead is not the top of its column"** fails a correct build, because at the skull's tapering
front corner it is both the top of its column and on a side face - and the side face is the whole
reason it reads. The property is that it faces OUTWARD.

### The visual audit: eight bearings, a value panel and a distance ladder

Rendered rather than reasoned about, and it found three things - one of which is a defect in
`gen/shell.py` that every future animal would have inherited.

**THE TAIL WAS 23% OF THE ANIMAL WHERE A REAL ONE IS ABOUT 38%.** Counted off the built model
station by station: head 8, body 24, tail and club 10. The profile silhouette read as a hedgehog
or an armadillo, because **the club is the feature that names this animal alongside the armour and
a club needs a length of tail to be on the end of.** At `tail_f -0.560L` and `club_f -0.610L` it is
32%, which is what a stranger reads as a clubbed tail. Two supporting measurements: the tail
necked to a SINGLE CELL at two stations before the club - the lollipop again, the join showing as a
stem between two masses - so its tip radius went up and the gap it has to be threaded across came
down; and the reservation had to follow, because `_CREATURE_ZHALF` was 24 while the animal now
reaches 27 rows back. **A stop that does not cover its own creature is a plinth with a tail hanging
off it**, and the clamp exists as a safety net for short spans rather than as a licence, so the
shipped `t` moved 0.25 -> 0.30 to keep it un-clamped.

#### `shell.py` WAS PAINTING A WARM ANIMAL GREEN, AND EUCLIDEAN DISTANCE CANNOT SEE IT

The plan - this animal's money view - came out mottled grey-green over a warm brown coat, and the
surface histogram says why: 5% of the visible cells were `mossy_stone_brick_slab` and
`mossy_stone_brick_stairs`. They are what `slab_for` picks for `dripstone_block`, which is the
