  three treads sat at 6**. It says a floor is lit when it is not, which is the whole failure the
  pass exists to prevent. The crop is gone: it propagates over the full canvas, which is what the
  test does anyway, **and the two agreeing is the point** - the same drift `proportions.measure` and
  `rubric.score` share an entry point to avoid.
- **THE FALLBACK BURIED THE LAMP UNDER THE FLOOR.** It searches `dy` in (0, -1, +1) so it can reach
  a neighbouring deck one course down - and on a flight, where every `dy=0` candidate is a stair, it
  took the STRINGER at `dy=-1` instead: a froglight sealed beneath an opaque deck block, placed,
  counted, lighting nothing. **A flush lamp must BE a floor**, so a candidate now has to have air
  over it. Nothing else in the code could see this: `put` succeeded, the grid was updated, the
  round reported progress.
- **AND RE-PLACING THE SAME LAMP COUNTED AS PROGRESS.** `got > 0` is the "nothing left I can reach"
  break, so choosing the same useless cell every round kept the solver alive for its whole
  24-round budget re-placing one lamp. A cell used once is not a candidate again, and with that the
  fixpoint converges in **4 rounds**.
- **THEN THE LAST RESORT HUNG A LANTERN OUT OF RANGE.** The gullet's climb is one cell wide with the
  animal's rock either side, so there is no floor to take and its ceiling is **eighteen courses up**
  - four more than a lantern reaches. It is chained down to four over the step now (`iron_chain`,
  not `chain`, in 26.x), which is the taproot entrance's own idiom for the same reason: light that
  falls DOWN a shaft rather than onto its rim. 14 chains, and the two "hanging from air" problems
  the flush version left went with them.

    286 transitions, 0 needing a jump . 0 steps over one course . 825 treads . 21 landings
    dark_left 0 in 4 rounds . 17 tests . 3,934 blocks . 0 new problems in context

#### AND A SLICE BETWEEN TWO ANCHORS DELETED TWO FUNCTIONS

Worth writing down because it cost more than any of the above. Replacing `_gullet` with
`b[:b.index('def _gullet(')] + new + b[b.index('def _prow('):]` silently deleted **`_runs`,
`_ribs` and `_bazaar`**, which lived between the two anchors - and the file is untracked, so there
was no git copy to recover from. It surfaced as `NameError: _bazaar is not defined` two builds
later.

**A slice replacement must be bounded by the END of the function being replaced, not by the next
anchor somebody remembers.** The safe form is to find the target's own terminator - the next
top-level `def` AFTER it - and assert that nothing else was removed by counting `def` before and
after.

### Still open

- **Nothing has been placed in game.** `render3d` has NO EMISSION, so the 144 froglights that are
  the entire reason anything down there is visible draw as cream blocks here. Judge form and mass
  off `out/market_*.png`; judge the light in world.
- **THE TWO EYE PODS ARE NOT REACHED, AND THE PRICE IS MEASURED.** 107 cells each, at Y172-182,
  one inside each eye - and a shaft from Prismworks lands on the crown with only TWO cells of shell
  over the left pod at X97558 Z80754, which is the best reveal available on this island: you
  descend eighteen blocks and arrive inside the squid's eye. What stops it is the other end - the
  cheapest internal bore from a pod to the main cavity is **27 solid cells** one wide, so a
  walkable 2x3 passage is roughly 150-200 dig cells through the head's own mass. That is a
  decision about digging into the sculpture, not a defect, and it is Jack's.
- **The arcade's deck is one flat plank field for 86 blocks.** The ribs give it a rhythm; a floor
  pattern would give it a grain.
- **The prow has TWO windows and the animal allows about that many.** A wider aperture needs a
  thinner wall than the mouth's ring has, and a forward one has nothing in its cone. If more light
  is wanted there it has to be put OUTSIDE - which is decorating the animal, and is Jack's call.
- `walk.ducked` is 4 - four Z values where the cavity leaves under three courses over a deck. They
  are at the tail taper and the walk closes over them; a fifth would be a hole.
- **The market is NOT in `Park Complete`.** Like the squid it ships at its own recorded origin, so
  `park_place.extras()` never lifts it to the park's build plane. Place it by name.

## The loop audit: every way the unattended build could sit still (2026-09-04)

Jack: *"do a deep audit of all aspects of the autonomous work flows, navigation, fetching, etc"*,
with two reports from the field: *"it doesnt get close enough to chests, chests need to be within
2 blocks"* and *"it seems to stack up with random resources vs things it logically might need
based on the radius around it"*. Three parallel audits — the router, the decision layer, the
material handling — came back with 68 findings; 40 are fixed here, all 591 Java tests pass, and
`AuditFixesTest` pins the ones that can be pinned without a client.

**THE SHAPE OF ALMOST EVERY DEFECT WAS THE SAME: A CLOCK THAT COULD NOT SEE A PHASE.** The stall
clock skips while fetching; the going-nowhere clock skips while fetching; the LOOK phase reset
its own target every recount. So a chest the flight parked short of, and a chunk that never
loaded, were both an infinite silent hover — the "does nothing, quietly" failure this file has
written rules about a dozen times, in the two phases none of those rules covered.

### The chest (Jack's first report) was three faults stacked

- **The approach cell was chosen NEAREST THE PLAYER**, up to 4.5 from the chest, and it moved as
  the player moved. `ContainerInteraction.approach` now ranks by distance to the CHEST — within
  two blocks preferred outright — and takes a set of cells already tried.
- **The flight could not descend to it.** `keepAirborne` holds the body 2.5 blocks off any floor,
  and chests stand on floors, so it hovered over the cell it was sent to and the opening test never
  passed. An approach cell must now have a clear cell UNDER it, and a target the body must actually
  occupy (`Hud.guideExact`) is flown with `EXACT_CLEAR` 1.05 — still over the block of air this
  server ends flight inside of — and an arrival ceiling of 1.6 instead of 3.0.
- **Nothing timed it out.** `FETCH_STUCK_MS` (6s parked, or the flight reporting arrival, with no
  opening ray) moves to the next approach cell; no cell left cools the chest off like an empty one.

### The pack (Jack's second report) was sized to the design

The shortfall was totalled over the WHOLE design and rotated 256 at a time across every material,
so a forty-material park filled the pack with whatever its far end wanted. `Plan.nearDemand` sizes
the fetch from the working anchor outward — the frontier first, then the nearest remaining cells
until they would fill the pack (`Work.loadCapacity`), and never a cell nothing can ever place.
The chest being flown to is latched for the trip, so two chests at nearly the same distance no
longer take turns being the target mid-flight.

### The router

- **A sloped leg was checked as a two-cell body at a rounded y.** Between courses the body is
  THREE cells tall; `clear` now spans floor(py+0.1)..floor(py+1.9). The old check passed a leg
  whose head went through a ceiling block, and `simplify` then straightened routes through it.
- **`escape` parked the body flush against the wall it was escaping** — the nearest cell to the
  goal is by definition the one touching the obstacle. A roomy cell (six clear neighbours) that
  improves at all is taken first; the flush one only inside a corridor, where nothing is roomy.
- **Staged and escape routes are PARTIAL, and were consumed as complete**: the flight reached the
  stage's end, flew DIRECT at the thing that had no route, and struck the spot for it. `Nav.Route`
  carries `complete`; `route()` returns complete routes only; the autopilot re-searches at the end
  of a stage and strikes only on `noRoute` — and strikes the SPOT CENTRE the loop filters by
  (`Hud.strikeKeyFor`), not the stand position fifty blocks from it that nothing looked up.
- **Staging was dead code** — the direct search spent the whole shared budget and staging broke
  on its first iteration. The direct search gets 60% when the goal is far.
- **A start cell the body did not fit in failed every search** (a slab, a carpet, a lip): the step
  box included the cell being left. The origin is excluded and an unfit start relaxes to the
  nearest fit cell.
- **`pocket`/`escape` marked a cell seen BEFORE the corner rule** rejected the step, so an L-bend
  read as a sealed pocket and the recovery ladder typed `/is` from inside a good corridor.
- **`reachable` broke ties by iteration order**, aiming at the far side of a chest in a wall about
  half the time. Ties go to the player's side.
- **Passability is the COLLISION SHAPE now, not `blocksMotion()`**: carpets and snow layers have a
  box the feet land on and no motion flag; an open door has the flag and nothing in the doorway.
- **One deadline for the roomy search, the tight search and the escape flood**; the stale-entry
  skip in A*; the deadline checked every 32 expansions rather than 256; `sees` cast from the eyes.
  A roomy route is simplified with the roomy predicate, or the chords threw the elbow room away.

### The loop

- **`follow all` shuttled between two FINISHED designs** — each read as "has work" because its
  cells were out of view from the other. Designs seen complete, handed back, or whose unseen cells
  would not load twice are never returned to; real work beats unseen-only.
- **DEAD_END, PACK_FULL and every-spot-ignored never advanced** under `follow all`. They park the
  design and move on. A `follow` that throws on the switch parks that design instead of dying.
- **A chunk unloading counted as placement** (todo shrank), inflating the report and blinding the
  thrash detector. Progress is the shrink `unseen` does not account for.
- **The going-nowhere clock fired with autofly OFF** every three seconds a manual follower paused;
  it is gated on the autopilot. STALL, the all-bins-tried retry and the cluster cap ejecting the
  current spot all go through `abandonSpot` now, so they count and are passed over.
- **A `Work.split` exception killed the loop silently** on the first hit — `following` stayed true
  with a null design. Three in a row stops properly and says so.
- **The printer's "never placeable" cache was never re-asked** while a design was followed; a wall
  torch judged before its wall existed stayed out of the frontier for the night. `Printer.relax`
  every 15 recounts.
- **A chest that WORKED was skipped for targeting** by the 5-second OK window (one map for two
  facts); `coolingOff` is failures only, `recentlyFailed` covers both. And the withdrawal's stop
  test counted boxed stock while the target handed to it did not, so a pack holding a shulker of
  the material took nothing and blacklisted a full chest.

### Placement and the things that ended the night

- **One missing placement ack ended the session.** It is a refusal of that cell and a slower pace;
  five in a row stop. Refusals ease the interval off, placements restore it.
- **A transfer whose answer never came ended the session**; the PACK is the truth, so the gain is
  counted from it, journalled UNCERTAIN, and only a run of three stops.
- **An OPENING failure left the chest GUI open**, which halts the autopilot, the loop and the
  printer until a human presses Escape. Our own screens are closed on failure and cancel.
- **The water bucket path was inert** — `BucketItem` overrides only `use()`, so `useItemOn` did
  nothing and every water cell was written off twice. It aims at the placement ray and uses
  `useItem`, and only where every horizontal neighbour and the cell below is already solid or
  water IN THE WORLD, or it pours the design's own basin away.
- **The printer placed nearest-first**, taking a ceiling before the wall that needed its face.
  It walks the design's own order and takes the first placeable cell in reach.
- **The digger dug nearest-first with whatever was held**: the Falls' notch — "cut it LAST" — could
  be cut first, and deepslate by hand passed a flat 120-tick give-up as "wrong tool". It digs in
  list order, never the last cell while another remains, holds the fastest hotbar tool, and gives
  up at twice the block's own expected time.
- **Unbox could only recover a box that landed within pickup range**, and searched three cells
  out; a site is adjacent, at foot level, with its lid cell clear. Soft failures no longer end the
  session; a box left out in the world does, through `Hud.stopForSafety`, which also clears the
  saved session so the next join does not resume into it.

**Deliberately not changed:** legacy index records with no dimension stay excluded from automatic
withdrawal — `BuildAuditTest` pins it as a rule, and it is one. Double chests are still indexed
per half and double-counted. `standoff`'s last-resort fallback still returns a cell the autopilot
cannot descend to (the station ladder handles it). None of this has been flown in game yet.

### Landing: work on a floor has no hovering stand (2026-09-04)

Jack, after the first jar: *"it is hovering above a group thats not placeable; i think we need
to also analyze area and identify when it can land and it should take off by itself"*.

**THE HOVER WAS STRUCTURAL.** A flying stand needs three clear cells under it (`Nav.AIR_BELOW`)
and the flight holds two and a half off any floor — both right for work on a wall, and both
impossible for work ON a floor: paving, a lawn, the bottom course of anything. Over a plate no
cell qualified, the fallback was the centroid, the flight parked three blocks over it, and the
printer reached nothing. Every station stalled, moved in closer (to another hover), abandoned,
and the next bin did the same. And it was worse than it looked: the stand's coverage was measured
from the FEET, so a stand four courses up "covered" paving its eyes were 4.6 blocks from, and a
stand UNDER the plate covered the paving on top of it, through the floor.

- **`Plan.groundStand`** — a cell the body fits in, with a real floor under it (a 3x3 pad, not a
  ledge over the void), that is not itself work still to place, from which the eyes are within
  reach of the most cells. `Hud.standAt` computes both stands and takes the ground when it
  covers at least as much as the air, because a body on a floor does not drift, holds no
  altitude, and cannot lose flight by touching something.
- **Coverage is from the EYES and only of cells the eyes can SEE** (`Plan.coveredFrom` with a
  `Passable`), for both kinds of stand. `Nav.sees` lost its "adjacent is always seen" shortcut,
  because the cell directly above the eyes' own ceiling is adjacent.
- **A landing is a target mode** (`Hud.Mode.LAND`). The flight descends onto the floor and lets
  flight end — on this server that is what contact does, and here it is the plan, so the
  mid-air-revocation emergency is suspended inside the last two and a half blocks. Arrival is
  standing on the cell.
- **It takes off by itself** through the existing double-tap (`Autopilot.regain`), now gated on
  `needsFlight`: a hovering station or a chest approach always needs the air; a landing does not
  if it can be WALKED to — a body standing beside the next patch of paving walks over, and only
  takes off when the walk is long (`WALK_AT_MOST` 24) or there is no walking route.
- **A landing that still reaches something of what is left is not re-aimed**: the orbit that
  moves a hovering station round its work would otherwise take off from a good floor because it
  placed something.

`tests/LandingTest.java` (5) and the rewritten `aSpotWithNoAirUnderItIsNotASpot` pin it: a
row of paving on a plate has no hovering stand and a landing that reaches it; a one-wide ledge
is not a floor; reach is the eyes' reach; the walk-or-fly rule.

**Not done, and worth knowing before the next flight:** the printer still needs the standing
body to have a line to each cell's face, and `groundStand` checks the eye line to the cell
centre, not to a face — a landing beside a cell whose only open face is away from it will stall
the station the usual way. And nothing here has been flown in game.

## The autofly fence: two corners, and it stays between them (2026-09-04)

Jack: *"lets edit auto fly so i can set two points and it only stays within those points."*
`Bounds.java`, `tests/BoundsTest.java` (11), and a bounds round-trip in `SessionTest`.

```
/cscan autofly bounds set                 the wand's two corners become the fence
/cscan autofly bounds <x1 y1 z1 x2 y2 z2> ...or six numbers
/cscan autofly bounds                     where it is, and whether you are inside it
/cscan autofly bounds off                 flight goes anywhere again
```

**THREE LAYERS, BECAUSE ANY ONE ALONE HAS A HOLE IN IT.** The PLAN filters cells and chests
outside the box out of the loop's own choices (`Hud`), so it never aims past the fence and works
the fenced area instead of stalling at its edge; the ROUTE wraps every passability predicate in
`Bounds.within`, so A* cannot find a way that leaves even to go round something; and the STEP is
clamped last, after `avoid`, on the flying step, the walk, and both recovery rungs, so the direct
guess, the unstick slide and the escape flood cannot carry the body past a face either. A body
already outside is pulled back in at 0.3 blocks a tick rather than flung. A destination outside
it - a `goto`, a photo bearing, a tidy source - holds and says so once, and `/cscan why` names it.

- **A FENCE IS NOT AN ACTIVITY**, so `/cscan stop` leaves it standing. It IS coordinates, so it
  clears on DISCONNECT and comes back from `session.json` only in the dimension it was drawn in -
  restored FIRST on resume, because a fenced loop that resumes unfenced is the dangerous direction.
- **A TELEPORT CANNOT BE FENCED.** The fall rescue keeps its `/is` - a fall is the inventory. The
  recovery ladder's GO_HOME rung is convenience and is withheld while a fence is set; it gives the
  spot up instead. Out-of-view cells outside the box are written off at once rather than after two
  look-watchdog strikes.
- **The one-course box has one legal height and it converges over two ticks**, not one - the
  return is speed-capped - which is what the first version of its test got wrong. And `holds` needs
  rounding slack: `(feet + step) clamped - feet`, re-added, is not exact.

Not flown in game yet. `bounds` and `set` went into `RESERVED`, which `SidecarSafetyTest` caught.

## The autonomy audit: three readers, 55 findings, 28 fixed (2026-09-04)

Jack: *"audit this and all autonomous functions deeply, we need this to be a seamless smooth system
that carefully guides the prints of entire schematics without getting caught or falling."* Three
parallel read-only audits - flight and routing, the loop's decisions, placement and materials -
then every finding verified against the code before it was touched. 632 Java tests, 0 failures.

**THE WORST FINDINGS WERE ALL "CORRECT ON THEIR OWN, WRONG TOGETHER"**, which is this file's own
recurring lesson at a larger scale:

- **THE TAKE-OFF COULD NEVER COMPLETE.** `regain()` (double-tap jump to get flight back) shared
  `rescueStage` with the fall rescue, which runs first every tick and resets that stage whenever
  the body is NOT falling. Stage 1 was wiped one tick after it began, so the key was held for four
  consecutive ticks - one jump, never a double tap - four tries were spent, and the session was
  permanently on foot. The landing mode shipped a day earlier depended on it. Own stage now.
- **A LANDED BODY NEVER MOVED AGAIN.** `needsFlight` said a landing within 24 blocks is WALKED,
  and `walk()`'s gate said only a FETCH may walk. Both rules are right; together no landing ever
  chained. The gate admits a landing, which is a floor by construction.
- **EVERY RECOVERY RUNG LASTED ONE TICK.** "Moving means fine" reset the ladder the moment the
  back-off's own first step moved the body, so the flight steered straight back into the wedge.
  While a rung drives, only the rung ends itself.
- **A ROUTED FLIGHT HAD NO FLOOR CLEARANCE AT ALL.** `Nav.of` keeps the two cells the body
  occupies clear and nothing below, so a tight route's cheapest leg skims a floor at 0.1 - and this
  server ends flight on contact. A LIFTED tier now sits between roomy and tight: a clear cell under
  the feet the whole way, tried before any route that may hug a floor. Indoors it fails at once.
- **`avoid()` TESTED AXES AND SENT THE DIAGONAL.** Each axis clear, the corner clipped. The
  combined step is tested and the smaller horizontal component is dropped first.

**The fence's own holes**, found the day after it shipped: stands, orbit stops and chest approach
cells were chosen with UNFENCED predicates, so the loop aimed at cells the autopilot then refused
and abandoned the spot (`Bounds.within` at all nine sites); `Bounds.within` wrapped a
`WalkingSpace` in a lambda and Nav lost the on-foot rules by type (`WalkingSpace.confined`);
`clamp` ran AFTER `avoid`, so a pull back into the box was never collision-tested (clamp first);
the Printer and Digger acted on cells outside the fence from inside it (the gate is at the
actuator now); the course lookahead and the re-anchor read the UNFILTERED todo, so eight courses
of fenced-out cells left fenced work one course up unreached (`eligible` is decided once).

**The loop's silent phases**: the dead end's second look path had no watchdog and no fence check
(one `lookForUnseen` for both sites); a completed look kept its strikes and its start time, so a
long look read as a 90s stall on arrival; a chunk loading with cells already BUILT counted as
placements (the printer's own report is the count now, the inference only while no chunk moved);
`Work.carrying` walked 41 slots so a block in the OFFHAND read as placeable stock; a dead end under
single `follow` idled all night (two minutes, then it stops and says so); the orbit index outlived
its ring; the hiccup stop did not write the session note; a foreign container screen parked the
loop in silence.

**The placement side**: `support()` let the printer right-click repeaters, comparators,
composters and bells - the server USES those before placing, so a repeater's delay cycled and
nothing went in (`Printer.toggles`); a water bucket used on a waterloggable kerb waterlogs the
KERB, which is a source flowing out of the pool; a half-placed double slab or multi-face vine was
judged a MISMATCH, given up and reported as a refusal (`Verdict.PARTIAL`); the hotbar swap evicted
whatever was selected - the digger's pickaxe - into the pack; a grass or fern cell was a
"deviation to break by hand" rather than something a right-click replaces; three journal I/O
failures called `Hud.off()` in silence and kept the note that resumes into the same failure.

**Deliberately NOT changed, stated:** chest approaches hover at 1.05 over the floor (the audit's
one worry, and the number Jack asked for); `hasArrived`'s wall-ahead rule; `Nav.standable` cannot
stand on carpet; `Printer.relax()` re-admits a twice-refused cell every 30s without back-off;
nothing here has been flown in game.

**And a working-practice note that cost an hour:** these Java files mix CRLF and LF WITHIN ONE
METHOD, and tabs with spaces on adjacent lines. A patch anchor with one newline style never
matches; the patcher that worked matches tokens with `\s+` between them.

## The friend island's corner stairs (2026-09-04)

`configs/friend_stair_{nw,ne,sw,se}.yaml`, `mcbuild/gen/arcstair.py`, `tests/test_arcstair.py`
(29). Jack, in three steps: *"alcoves cut with slabs, want to put spiral staircases on each end
of the slab which then meet at a lower center point combining into a single staircase"*; then
*"instead i want to connect two ends, so that they circle and meet in the center of where the
multiple water streams are"*; and *"the stairs are symmetrical in materials etc, they should be
duplicate and then meet in the middle"*. Materials are the platform's own: spruce slabs, stone
brick.

**The site, measured off `friendisland` (in `out/`, bedrock box origin -22421 -64 -97421):** a
round deck of spruce TOP slabs at Y198 (surface 199.0) over open void, centre cell
(-22400, -97400) where the log spokes cross, a cobblestone house on it, and a 2x2 notch framed
in stone-brick top slabs on either flank of each arm's tip - eight notches, the north-west pair
at u,v offsets [-16..-15, -5..-4] and its mirror, every other corner a sign flip. **Between
neighbouring arms a two-wide waterfall falls along the diagonal from Y198 to bedrock** - 70
columns, its outer row at r 14.8-16.2 from the centre - and every one is refused at every
course, because a tread under falling water catches it and spreads it seven cells over the
stair. The east-north notch is missing its three outer deck cells in this capture.

**Per corner: 451 blocks, 0 problems, 0 overlap, ONE piece with the platform, all cheap, both
flights mirror cell for cell and block for block (`asymmetric_cells: 0`), and it WALKS from the
pad through both notches to the deck under the audit's own rules.** The four notch cells become
bottom slabs a half step down; from each notch an ARC of eight treads follows the rim at
r 17-19.5 - OUTSIDE the curtain - one 3.26-degree sector per half step, a stone-brick block for
a whole-number surface and a spruce slab on a stone-brick stringer for a half one; the two arcs
end flat on the diagonal at 194.5 against a landing of stone-brick slabs on a solid 3x3 pier
standing 21 out along the diagonal, in the curtain's middle; a slab helix winds ten courses down
round the pier to a stone pad, because nothing is below it yet. `/cscan place "Friend Stair NW"`
by NAME - they are not in `sync.yaml`, whose captures are the main island's.

**THE SECOND FLIGHT IS THE FIRST REFLECTED, NOT THE FIRST REBUILT.** It is laid with the same
sectors on mirrored angles, the tread rhythm is fixed by HEIGHT (block, slab, block, slab) and
never by a per-cell hash, and the mirror is then measured over every cell above the landing and
written to the sidecar. A duplicate that is asserted is a duplicate; one that is merely likely
drifts the first time a hash or a world cell differs.

Five things that shipped `problems: 0` and were wrong, each caught by a walk or a component count:

- **THE COURSES JUST UNDER A TOP-SLAB DECK HAVE NO HEADROOM.** The audit wants two clear cells
  over ceil(surface), so the flight leaves the notch OUTWARD, off the rim, and never runs under
  the deck. (The first design, twin helices hung under the arm, spent its top five half-steps
  finding open sky for exactly this reason.)
- **A FLIGHT WITH NO POST IS CONNECTED ONLY IN COURSE-MATE PAIRS.** A bottom slab and the block a
  course down beside it are diagonal neighbours - walkable, and not one piece. The stringer under
  every slab tread is what makes the arc a solid.
- **A PIER'S BOTTOM COURSE HAS A SURFACE TOO, AND IT IS COVERED.** `audit.check_climb` started its
  walk at the lowest surface in the model, tied with the pad, and by x-then-z tie-break began
  inside the masonry on two corners of four - a walkable stair reported unclimbable. It starts on
  the lowest surface a player can STAND on now; nothing that passed before can fail by it.
- **A HELIX BUILT OF BLOCKS AND STRINGERS RENDERS AS A LUMP.** The descent has the pier to hang
  from, so it is slabs only (bottom, then top), which is what a slab helix is for.
- **THE PROBE MUST SCORE THE WALK, NOT THE CELL COUNT.** The descent's start and spin are tried
  sixteen ways; scored by cells placed, the winner's third wedge was empty and the walk died
  under the landing. Scored by the longest walkable chain, it does not.

`render3d` cannot judge the palette; judge form here (`out/friend_orbit.png`) and colour in world.

## The trip leaves from the work and comes back to it (2026-09-04)

Jack: *"autofly etc basically infinitely wanders fetching small amounts of shit, finding
somewhere to put it, often failing to put it, coming back, repeating infinitely, its highly
inefficient, chaotic, and doesnt check inventory, area, or fill inventory based on needs at
all."* Every clause of that is one defect, and they were all the same defect: **the loop had no
idea where the work was once it left it.**

    the working area      focus(eligible, ME, radius)        me = the chest, mid-fetch
    the shopping list     nearDemand(eligible, frontier, ME) re-sized every recount, at the chest
    the trip's end        canWork, measured where I stand    "nothing placeable" at a store hall
    out of view           todo empty -> LOOK                 mid-trip, then back to the trip
    the pack              loadCapacity = empty slots         never emptied of anything

So a fetch flew to the store hall, re-planned the load for the cells nearest the STORE HALL,
came back to those cells rather than to the spot it had left, found nothing placeable, read
that as a dead end or a reason to shop again, and did it all with a pack that a previous design's
leftovers had shrunk to a stack or two of room. Nothing in `LoopTest` could see it, because the
phase function is right for every combination of its inputs and the inputs were being measured
in the wrong place.

- **`Hud.workAnchor`.** Set to the nearest work on the first recount, moved to the spot being
  built as it drifts, moved deliberately when an area is finished (to the nearest remaining cell
  to the AREA, so the work walks across the design) or when the loop goes to look at unseen
  cells - and never by a fetch. The working area is `focus(eligible, anchor, radius)`. When the
  anchor's chunk is not loaded and the loop is not mid-trip, it goes BACK there and decides
  nothing until it arrives.
- **`Plan.loadPlan`: the shopping list is made ONCE, at the work, and held for the trip.** In
  BUILD ORDER: the frontier first, then the area's cells lowest course first and nearest the
  anchor within a course, up to what the pack can hold. Sorted by 3D distance instead, the pack
  filled with roof for a wall whose ground course still wanted stone. `Plan.shortfalls` is the
  list minus what is carried, with addresses; the amount taken is the list's, not four stacks.
- **`Loop.phase`: a trip with somewhere still to go is not interrupted by the work going out of
  view.** `todo == 0` with cells unseen used to mean LOOK, mid-trip too: the chunks under the
  anchor unloaded on the way to the chest, the loop turned round to look at them, then turned
  round again to finish the trip. That is the ping-pong.
- **`Work.dumpable`: the pack is CHECKED, and what it holds for no reason is put away.** A stack
  that places a block, holds nothing itself, and is wanted by no cell of the WHOLE design goes
  into the chest the trip is at before anything comes out of it (`Withdraw` deposits by the same
  shift-click and reconciles it the same way, one stack a pass). Never a tool, food, a bucket or
  a shulker box; never a material for the far end. Those slots count as room when the list is
  sized, so a pack full of the last design reads as a full trip rather than as PACK_FULL. A full
  chest stops the putting-away and says so; nothing is ever dropped.
- **The trip ends where it ends, and then goes home.** When the phase leaves FETCH with the
  anchor out of view, the loop flies back to the anchor rather than deciding anything about the
  chest's surroundings.

`/cscan why` now says the anchor (and whether it is loaded), the shopping list of the trip in
progress, and what is in the pack for no reason. `PackTest` (5) pins the dumping rule,
`AuditFixesTest` the build-order list and the shortfalls, `LoopTest` the uninterrupted trip.
**652 Java tests, 0 failures.** `chunkscan-0.8.1.jar` is built and not uploaded.

**Not flown in game**, and two things to watch when it is: the deposit is a shift-click INTO a
chest through the same reconciliation as taking, which has been exercised offline only; and
"often failing to put it" is the printer's refusal path, which this pass does not touch beyond
sending the loop back to the spot it left - if refusals persist AT the anchor, that is the next
audit and it is a different subsystem.

## Baritone reads a litematic's air as MUST-BE-AIR, and the loop's three audits (2026-09-05)

Jack, trying Baritone's builder on a design: *"baritone says the schematic has 101 air blocks
treated as physical"*. The exact wording is not in any installed jar or in `latest.log` (client
messages are not logged), so the number is unexplained; the MECHANISM is not, and it is worse than
the message.

**A LITEMATIC CANNOT EXPRESS "DON'T CARE", AND BARITONE READS EVERY AIR CELL INSIDE A REGION AS A
PLACEMENT TO SATISFY.** Read off `BuilderProcess.valid()` and `assemble()` rather than remembered:
only a cell outside every sub-region is `null` (skipped); a desired `air` with a world block under
it goes into `breakable`. Our designs are REMAINING WORK padded to `origin_lock` - one region of
mostly air lying over the finished island - so fed as they stand Baritone digs the world back to
the design's air. Measured with `mcbuild baritone <design> --world <capture>`: the four Friend
Stairs sit over **1,064 / 2,159 / 2,118 / 4,111** blocks of the platform they hang off.

```
python -m mcbuild baritone "Friend Stair NW" --world friendisland --copy
```
prints the three settings that make the design additive, off Baritone's own `Settings.java`:
`#buildSkipBlocks air` ("a list of blocks to be treated as correct"), `#buildIgnoreExisting true`
("will only place new blocks"), `#allowBreak false` (the guarantee under the other two) - plus
`#buildInLayers true`, `#layerOrder false` and `#startAtLayer <lowest unbuilt course>`, the exact
`#build <file> x y z` line from the sidecar's origin (every region we write sits at Position
0,0,0, so the min corner IS the origin), and the dig count. Two things it had to know:
**`startAtLayer` is schematic-relative** (Jack's `settings.txt` had 199, which on `Park Complete`
- origin Y94 - is world Y293), and **`#build` reads ONE token as the file**, so `Park
Complete.litematic` is looked up as `Park`; `--copy` writes a space-free twin. Baritone itself
lives in the LiquidLauncher profile's `mods/` (`Baritone.jar`, 26.2-1.11.1), not in `custom_mods`.
`tests/test_baritone.py` (3) pins the dig count, the settings and the copy.

### The audit: three readers over 20k lines, 23 fixes, and what a printer would look like

Jack: *"so many issues with its item seeking, movement, etc, it needs to be a printer - we need
to be organized, and not get stuck."* Three parallel read-only audits (decision layer, movement,
materials) against the in-flight tree, each finding verified in the code before it was touched.
**The single worst finding was in that day's uncommitted work**: `AutomationControl.enter`
refused any WITHDRAW unless `BuildJob.phase == FETCH`, and ChestScan (at a DEAD_END) and Unbox
(mid-BUILD) both open chests outside FETCH - so `Withdraw.tick` never ran its own timer, `busy()`
was true for ever, `Hud.advance` returned early ABOVE every clock, and the body hovered at the
chest in silence until `/cscan stop` (Unbox worse: the shulker left on the ground). **The job
phase gates the PRINTER and nothing else now.**

Fixed, each with the reason in the code:

- **The anchor did not survive a trip.** Back at the store hall with the work unloaded, the
  look-for-unseen ran first and `goLook` re-anchored on the unseen cell nearest the PLAYER; or
  the radius grew to reach whatever was loaded round the chest and a spot formed there. The
  shopping list sized at the work then came back somewhere else - "fetches, comes back, fails
  to place". The look and the radius growth both wait while the anchor is unloaded.
- **"Back to the work" had no give-up**: an anchor whose chunk never loads was guided to every
  two seconds for ever, and the 90s stall struck nothing because there was no spot. `RETURN_MS`
  (45s) or an Ignored anchor drops it and re-anchors; a stall with no spot strikes the target.
- **`Printer.relax()` manufactured a false frontier every 30s**: clearing the placeability cache
  outright made every cell past the 400-per-recount budget read as placeable again, so cells the
  printer had proved impossible came back as the frontier, a station was chosen on them, nothing
  placed, the spot struck. The old verdicts are kept as the fallback until re-asked.
- **`LAYER_LOOKAHEAD = 8` turned real work into a DEAD_END**: eight courses of printer-refused
  cells (lanterns waiting on posts, vines) emptied the frontier with work one course higher, and a
  dead end on a design with unseen cells goes to LOOK elsewhere - the wandering. Every course.
- **A-B-A ping-pong ran all night**: `avoidSpot` held ONE spot so B's abandonment un-avoided A,
  and one block placed per leg reset the thrash count. It is a map with expiry, and fewer than
  `THRASH_TRICKLE` (5) blocks between abandonments is nothing placed.
- **One 25ms clock for every route tier** let the first search that fails BY BUDGET spend it all:
  beside a row of shops the safe tiers fail that way as a matter of course, the tight search that
  finds the indoor route got ~30 nodes, and "no route and no way round" was the clock. Each tier
  has its own slice (`CRUISE_SHARE`..`TIGHT_SHARE`, ordered and pinned).
- **A ROUTE WAS THE ONE THING THAT BYPASSED THE GROUND CLEARANCE.** Roomy keeps one block of air
  off a floor; this server has ended flight at a block's distance, which is why `GROUND_CLEAR` is
  2.5 - and the routed step skips that clamp on purpose (indoors it grinds the ceiling). A CRUISE
  tier is searched first: roomy AND `CRUISE_BELOW` (3) clear under the body, relaxed within `ENDS`
  of either end, so a flight over the plate stays at the hover's own height.
- **A waypoint popped early chorded the corner it was there to round**: at cruise the radius is
  ~1.9, `legFrom` jumped ahead of the body, and the pursuit aimed along a leg the body had not
  reached - a line `clear` never validated, at every shop corner. `popped()` pops early only once
  the body is PAST the plane through the waypoint perpendicular to the next leg.
- **The recovery ladder belonged to no destination**: `trouble` was never reset when the target
  changed, so a new station inherited the last wedge; and CLIMB_OUT ended at `trouble =
  BACK_OFF_AT`, so it re-entered at back-off, climbed again, and never reached GO_HOME - 25 blocks
  up each time. Reset per destination; a second climb gives the spot up instead.
- Stale state on `follow`: `deadEndSince`, `unboxRetryAt`, the orbit leg.

**Still open, from the same audits and NOT guessed at** - each is a decision or a subsystem:

- **The chest approach hovers at 1.1 blocks of air** (`HOVER_CLEAR + FOOT_OFFSET`) against the
  2.5 the plugin has been measured to need, because Jack asked for "within 2 blocks". Either the
  fetch becomes a deliberate LANDING beside the chest, or the number is his to confirm in game.
- **Landing is one-way unless the server keeps `mayfly`**: `regain` gives up after four taps and
  never types `/fly`. `/fly` is a TOGGLE, so it is only safe when `!mayfly` - untested here.
- **A chest outside render distance is blacklisted before the flight starts** (`fetchTo` asks
  `approach()` of an unloaded chunk and reads null as "nowhere to open it from") - so the loop
  only ever fetches from chests already loaded near the work.
- **The frontier and the printer disagree about three block kinds**: replaceable plants (in todo,
  refused by `placement()`), water pools two cells wide (`contained()` deadlocks), door hinges.
  Each is a silent station stall, not a refusal.
- **Litematic state strings carry every property and `StateContract` treats world-derived ones
  as REQUIRED** (`age`, `berries`, `thickness`, `chest type`, `snowy`...) - the Python side's
  `work.INTENTIONAL` filter, not applied on the Java read.
- **The shopping list is sized to the lowest course within a radius that can grow to 200**, so
  in a three-level park it fills with the undercroft's blackstone while the surface is paved; and
  `loadCapacity` counts every slot as 64 (a pool of water asks for one bucket per cell).
- **Double chests are indexed twice** (151 pairs live); the stale twin sends the loop back.
- **`Work.split` runs over all 540,862 cells every TICK while printing**, and the journal fsyncs
  twice per placement. That stutter is part of what reads as freezing at chests.
- **A printer-mode rewrite of the spot logic** - one ordered queue per course, next bin in sweep
  order rather than fullest, refusals per bin, the shopping list = the next N bins - is the shape
  all three audits converged on. It replaces `Plan.clusters`/`Loop.sameSpot`/`stand` and is a
  session of its own.

**Nothing here has been flown in game.** 654 Java tests green (652 at the start of the session); `chunkscan-0.8.1.jar` not rebuilt.

Two working-practice notes: **the Bash tool fails with `unexpected EOF` on scripts past ~100
lines** - write the script with the Write tool and run the file; and **a whitespace-tolerant
patch anchor must start at its first TOKEN**, or `\s+` swallows the newline before it and the code
lands on the end of the comment above - twice in one session, both compile errors.

### Two more, on Jack's next two notes (same day)

**"It shouldn't be pulling things out of chests if it has a 90% inventory of a single item."**
The fetch decision asked only about the LOWEST COURSE near the anchor, so a pack of stone brick
beside a course of slabs read as "nothing I can place" and became a trip for one stack of slabs;
and the top-up at every session start asked no question about the pack at all. `Loop.WORK_LOAD`
(four stacks) is a working load: carrying that much of a material the design still wants, the loop
builds it first - no top-up if the frontier course has cells for it, a higher course near the
anchor becomes the frontier if that is where they are, and if they are elsewhere in the loaded
design it re-anchors there rather than opening a chest. Only when nothing carried can be placed
anywhere loaded is a chest worth the trip. `LoopTest` pins the predicate.

**"If I type moss_block it only does that material until it's filled every potential place of
it on the schematic."** `/cscan only moss_block` (one or more item names; `off` lifts it). Every
cell of another material is not the session's work: filtered out of the frontier, the shopping
list and the PRINTER's own in-reach pick, so a pack of slabs places nothing while the filter is
set. The session ends - stopped, and said, never "complete" - when no loaded cell of the material
is left and every chunk has been seen. The filter rides in `session.json` and is restored FIRST on
resume, because a resumed `follow` that forgot it would place everything. `Loop.itemName`
normalises `minecraft:`, case and a `[state]`; it is the ITEM name, so `stone_brick_slab` is both
halves and every facing.

**And the chest approach hovered at one block of air** (`HOVER_CLEAR` 1, `EXACT_CLEAR` 1.05) -
the one place the body was flown to exactly the height this server ends flight at, on the
reasoning that 2.5 would put a floor chest out of reach. It would not: from two clear cells up the
eyes are ~3.4 from a chest one block over, inside `Withdraw.REACH`. Two now, and a routed step
keeps the ground clearance whenever the next waypoint itself has it - the bypass stays only for
routes that genuinely go low. `AuditFixesTest` re-derives the reach arithmetic.

**`chunkscan-0.8.2.jar` is built** (`build/libs/`), 656 Java tests green, not uploaded - Jack
uploads through the launcher himself. Nothing in it has been flown yet.

### 0.8.3: it stays where the work is, and it flies over the top (same night)

Jack flew 0.8.2 - every fix above was in it - and reported the same two things in sharper words:
*"its path finding and flying is still really bad, constant collisions, running right into
objects"*, and *"if its actively placing idk why it keeps instantly seeking and then flies off ...
sometimes it has a massive patch, will place 5, then go fly away from it ... it should look in
its immediate vicinity and just keep placing as much as possible always."*

**THE STATION WAS RE-CHOSEN EVERY RECOUNT AS THE FULLEST BIN.** Place five blocks and another bin
is the fullest; the flight left with work still in reach, and every flight is a chance to touch
something. `Loop.holdHere` runs BEFORE any question about anchors, courses, spots or stations:
while anything placeable that I carry is within `Loop.VICINITY` of the body, guidance is dropped
and the printer places on its own tick. The hold ends only when nothing in reach is left, or when
it has held for `STATION_MS` with nothing placed - then the station machinery gets its turn and the
hold is disarmed for `HOLD_COOL_MS`, or it wins the next recount straight back.

**AND THE ROUTER IS NO LONGER HOW A LONG LEG IS FLOWN.** Every collision in a day of router fixes
was a flight THROUGH built space - between shops, under awnings, past corners - and each fix made
the threading a little better without making it safe. A player with /fly goes UP, crosses in open
sky, and comes DOWN. `Autopilot.overTop` builds exactly that for any leg over `OVERTOP_MIN` (4)
blocks: the corridor's highest MOTION_BLOCKING surface (heightmap, margin 2 each side) plus
`OVERTOP_CLEAR` (3) is the crossing height, never below where the body already is; three
waypoints, each leg verified with `Nav.clear`; NEVER simplified (the chord from the ascent's foot
to the descent's head is the diagonal through the buildings it exists to fly over). A roofed
descent stops on the roof and the router does the last few blocks, which is the one place it has
ever been good; a ceiling over the ascent hands the whole leg to the router. The heightmap answers
the world's own minimum for an unloaded chunk, so an unseen tall building raises the crossing as
its chunk arrives, and the blind-speed rule still covers the approach.

`AutopilotTest` pins the legs and the height arithmetic; `LoopTest` the hold. 658 Java tests
green, `chunkscan-0.8.3.jar` built, not flown.

### 0.8.4: the scan that ran twenty times a second (2026-09-06)

Jack: *"it also scans too frequently, i think it uses a full radius based on current position vs
set positions."* It did. The printer's tick asked `Work.split` for the cells within reach of the
body, and `split` answered by walking ALL 540,862 cells of the park - a distance test each - and
re-parsing the design's sidecar JSON for the dig list, on every call, twenty times a second. That
is the stutter that reads as freezing at chests and as jerky flight.

- **The work list is BINNED BY CHUNK when it is loaded**, cached with the list and the dig list.
  A radius question touches only the chunks the radius covers (`Work.binNear`, a box test per
  bin), and an unloaded chunk costs one `hasChunk` with its cells counted unseen, rather than a
  world lookup per cell. The HUD's full recount every two seconds skips the unloaded 80% of the
  park the same way.
- **A placement sweep that found no angle is not re-run every tick** for ten ticks
  (`Printer.recentlyUnplaceable`): yaw by pitch by face for every in-reach cell that fails was the
  other half of the tick.
- **No fsync per placement.** Two disk syncs per block (attempt, verdict) were up to forty
  milliseconds on the client thread each time; `reconcile()` already survives a torn last line.
- **And the vicinity hold targets the body's own cell**, not "no target": with no target the
  autopilot said "autofly is ON but has nowhere to go" at every hold, and would have lifted a
  landed body off good paving.

659 Java tests green, `chunkscan-0.8.4.jar` built, not flown.

### 0.8.5: the open list, closed (2026-09-06)

Jack: *"fix all."* The items the audits had left as decisions, each now taken:

- **A chest out of view is flown to, not blacklisted.** `fetchTo` asked `approach()` of an
  unloaded chunk, read null as "nowhere to open it from" and cooled the chest for a minute - so
  the loop could only ever fetch from chests already loaded near the work. It flies toward the
  chest now and picks the approach cell once the chunk is here.
- **Only DECIDED properties have to match.** `StateContract.role` is the Python side's
  `work.INTENTIONAL` on the Java read, plus four this side keeps as completion requirements
  (`waterlogged`, `powered`, `persistent`, `open`) and a rail's `shape`. Before, `sugar_cane
  [age=7]`, `cave_vines[berries]`, `chest[type=left]`, `grass_block[snowy]` had to match exactly:
  the cell silently left the frontier, or placed correctly and was reported WRONG STATE.
- **A double chest is one record**, filed under its lower half (`Storage.canonical`, from
  `ChestBlock.FACING`/`TYPE`); the stale twin of an old record is dropped by `stillThere`.
- **Flight revoked by the server is asked back**: `regain` sends `/fly` (bounded to three per
  destination) while `mayfly` is FALSE - the one state in which a toggle can only go on - then
  double-taps as before; and the tries reset per destination rather than per session.
- **A replaceable block is placed into**: grass, ferns and snow layers were in todo and refused by
  `placement()`, a silent station stall with no refusal ever reported.
- **A pool wider than one cell can be placed**: `contained()` accepts a neighbour that is the
  design's own water (`Printer.setDesignWater`, from the followed design), and flowing water in
  the cell is not "a block in the way". The rim still has to be solid.
- **A bucket is not a stack**: a shopping list asks for at most `Plan.BUCKETS_PER_TRIP` (4).

662 Java tests green, `chunkscan-0.8.5.jar` built, not flown. The one thing here that touches
a server command is `/fly`, and it is only ever sent while the server itself says flight is off.

### `analyze`: what a build can TAKE today, not what it is made of (2026-09-06)

Jack: *"analyze schematics automatically, identify most used materials, and most placeable based on
no air blocks around it based on currently placed, so we can efficiently spread resources in large
builds."* A bill of materials answers the wrong question for a trip: a pack of the commonest block
is a pack with nothing to place against, if the commonest block is the roof.

```
python -m mcbuild analyze "Park Complete" --world newisle --have     # offline, against a capture
/cscan analyze <design>                                              # in game, against the live world
```

Per material: **placeable** (remaining cells with a clickable face-neighbour standing), **unlocks**
(cells that cannot go in yet which a placeable cell of this material would give a face to), left,
stacks, have/short against the container index, and the 16-region holding the most placeable
cells. Ranked placeable first. On a fresh Friend Stair the answer is eight slab cells - the notches
- and nothing else, which is exactly right: everything else hangs off them.

**And the loop's shopping list is led by it.** `Plan.loadPlan` used to lead with the frontier
course only; it leads with EVERY placeable cell near the anchor on any course now (`Plan.usable`
is the same ranking as a list), so the trip that comes back places the most and opens the most.

**Clickable is the printer's rule, not the audit's.** The first offline pass counted only full
cubes as something to place against and called every cell of the stair unplaceable: the friend
platform is top slabs. `analyze.clickable` mirrors `Printer.support` by name - a slab, a stair, a
wall, a chest is a face; a vine, a tuft, a torch, a carpet, a rail, water is not. `tests/test_
analyze.py` (2) and `PlanTest` pin the ranking: 20 placeable planks outrank 300 wool of roof.

663 Java tests green, `chunkscan-0.8.5.jar` includes the command.

## A DIAGONAL JOIN IS NOT A JOIN: `printable` (2026-09-06)

Jack: *"a lot of the schematic has blocks that are diagonal to each other but hollow, meaning it's
impossible to print on them since there's nothing attached to any one side of them ... they may
have a line of things, but the entire line is diagonal so nothing reaches it when printed below or
from above."* Every word of that was measurable and none of it was measured.

    python -m mcbuild printable "Park Complete"                # what a printer can never reach
    python -m mcbuild printable "Park Complete" --fix          # ...and close the corners

**A PRINTER CLICKS A FACE, SO PRINTABILITY IS A CLOSURE OVER 6-CONNECTIVITY, SEEDED BY THE WORLD.**
That is a different question from every check this project had. `audit.check_supports` asks whether
a block can EXIST; `pipeline._floating` asks whether a cell has anything under it; `analyze` asks
what can go in TODAY. None of them asks whether the chain ever arrives, and a design can pass all
three while being unbuildable.

Measured on the shipped `Park Complete` - 540,862 cells:

| | |
|---|---|
| separate printing islands | **2,009** - each one a block a human must place by hand |
| cells a printer could NEVER reach | **18,721 (3.5%)** |
| ...orphaned by a DIAGONAL rather than genuinely floating | **16,062** |
| the largest single casualty | the **14,393-cell undercrypt**, whose only contacts with the rest of the park are (1,1,1) corners |

**THE FAULT IS TINY AND THE DAMAGE IS NOT**, which is the whole reason this is a pass rather than
something to eyeball: **889 corner fills returned 15,597 cells**, and the undercrypt came back for
about ten blocks. 18,721 unreachable -> 3,129, islands 2,009 -> 1,913.

### What a stitch is allowed to be

- **A CORNER FILL, NEVER A SCAFFOLD.** `REACH` is 2 because a two-axis diagonal needs ONE cell and
  a three-axis one needs TWO. Anything further is a bridge, and a lump of blocks alone in the void
  is REPORTED rather than reached - that one is a person with a stack of dirt, and inventing it
  here would hide the finding that matters under a pile of invented terrain.
- **It never covers anything.** Only cells empty in BOTH the design and the world, which is the one
  property that makes it safe to run over a build somebody is halfway through.
- **Its material is the commonest clickable, NON-FALLING material already touching it** -
  `deckfloor`'s heal rule, so a stitch cannot introduce a block the design was not already
  spending, and rule 13 cannot be broken by a fill that is over air by construction.
- **Of the two corners that close a step, it takes the one UNDER the upper block.** That is a
  STRINGER - the course the arc stair and every flight in this project build by hand - and not a
  lump on a finished surface. 615 of 889 land that way; the rest have only one legal corner.
- **A cell a player could stand in is a last resort and is COUNTED.** A fill in a doorway is the
  fault this repo has shipped three times (a timber set on a live rail, an adit's post bricking up
  its own corridor, two pines in the one walk a module exists to carry). 121 landed in one, so the
  walk was flooded before and after: **105,397 cells reachable from the gate, both times.**

**AND IT IS INVISIBLE IN PRACTICE, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME AS BURIED.** Jack asked for the fills to
be *"pretty much always invisible... placed on the inside of hollow objects"*, and measured
literally only 44 of 889 are sealed inside the build - the park is 95% open air, and a diagonal
join is by its nature on a SURFACE (a helix's rim, a stair's corner), so there is usually no buried
option to choose. What settles it is a render: the densest cluster - **175 fills in one 44-cube** -
is indistinguishable from the original at all eight bearings, because a one-block fill in the notch
of a rough surface reads as nothing. Judge this one by looking, not by the exposure count.

### What is left, and why it is not stitched

    1,062  the Prism Well descent, Y105-205    hanging in an open shaft, 3,409 air neighbours
       35  a birch at X97500 Y204-210          a tree whose trunk never reaches the ground
      ~12  x6 lamp standards, Y203-210         a base at Y203 with no lawn under it at Y202
    1,716  pond and plant dressing             lily pads, seagrass, vines, water surfaces

**THE DRESSING IS REPORTED APART AND MUST BE.** A lily pad is placed against WATER and a vine
against a leaf, so the closure cannot chain through either - correctly - and calling two thousand
single cells of pond furniture "unprintable masses" would bury the one real finding. `DECOR` names
them and `Survey.split_unfixable` separates them; **a solid block filled into a pond is not a
repair, it is a filled pond.**

The descent is the one structural hole left and it is a DESIGN decision, not a stitch: a helix in
an open shaft whose lining stops at Y187 has nothing to attach to at any reach.

### Where it runs

**`tools/park_place.py` stitches the composite at the moment it writes it**, because a break
BETWEEN two modules belongs to neither and no generator or per-design pass can see it - the same
reason `finish.carve_for` became a pipeline step rather than a note. A step that has to be
remembered is a step that gets lost, and this file has recorded that once already.

`tests/test_printable.py` (18) pins the shape rather than a snapshot: a diagonal line is one island
per block, a straight one is one island, a carpet carries nothing onward, a stitch never covers,
never falls, and hides under its tread - and **the shipped composite has no diagonal break a corner
fill could still close**. Asserting a cell COUNT would be the snapshot trap this repo has now
recorded five times; asserting "nothing the pass could fix is still open" cannot go stale.

**Two things worth keeping for whoever runs this next.** The three park plot captures
(`islandleft`, `newisle`, `islandright`) are **bare starter pads - 189, 144 and 192 blocks** - so
the park prints onto void and a survey against any one of them reads the other two lands as
unreachable; composite them with `coop.merge_scans` first, or run with no world at all, which seeds
from the design's own largest mass and answers in ISLANDS. And a per-module survey is the wrong
context by construction: `PF Park Green` reads as 2,599 islands alone because every flower stands
on `Park Ways`' ground, which is a different design. Rule 2, in a new place.

## The frame rate, and the bot that dug itself in (2026-09-06, chunkscan 0.8.6)

Jack: *"its scanning too fast, you start autofly and its supremely laggy, basically no frames per
second"*, and separately *"we also need to make sure the bot doesnt dig itself into a hole - its
multiple times now sat still and dug completely around itself. If it starts to have sides of itself
covered, e.g. 2/3 sides of body, it should move up etc to start avoiding being stuck."*

### THE RECOUNT WAS THE FREEZE, AND EVERY LINE OF IT LOOKED CHEAP

`Hud` recounts the followed design every 40 ticks with `Work.split(..., radius 0)` - **the whole
design, which on `Park Complete` is 540,862 cells**. That much is by design and has to be: the loop
needs global counts to know it is finished. What was not by design is what each cell cost, and all
four of these are one-line call sites that read as free:

| per cell, ~270,000 times a recount | was |
|---|---|
| `StateContract.parse` | `synchronized`, over an **access-ordered `LinkedHashMap`** - which REWRITES ITS LINKED LIST ON EVERY GET. Every lookup was a structural mutation under a monitor |
| `Work.matches` | `BuiltInRegistries.BLOCK.getKey(st.getBlock()).getPath()` - a registry lookup and a substring, per cell |
| `ActionRecipe.order` | **the sort key**, and it parsed the state string and allocated a `HashMap` every call. In a comparator over ~100,000 cells that is about **3.5 MILLION** parses and allocations per recount |
| `Printer.props` | the same parse again, under `order`, `doubleSlab` and the placement sweep |

Plus `digLeft` walked **all 9,846 dig cells** with `isLoaded` + `getBlockState` on every `split` -
and `split` runs on **every printer tick**, so a bound that exists to keep work local was costing
two hundred thousand world lookups a second to produce a list of nothing.

All four are memoised now (a design has a few hundred distinct block states, so it is one parse
each, ever), the sort is DECORATE-SORT-UNDECORATE so the key is computed once per cell rather than
twice per comparison, and `digLeft` takes the radius and filters BEFORE it asks the world - a
distance test is free and a chunk lookup is not.

**AND THE CACHE THAT CAUSED IT WAS SOMEBODY'S FIX FOR SOMETHING ELSE.** An LRU is the obvious shape
for "cache the last N", and an access-ordered `LinkedHashMap` is the obvious LRU - and its eviction
policy costs a WRITE ON EVERY READ, which is the opposite of what a read-mostly cache wants. Both
new caches are bounded and simply stop filling: a world with more distinct states than the cap gets
no caching, which is exactly what it had before.

### `/cscan perf` - because this was diagnosed by reading the code three times

`Perf.java`, and it is the honest lesson of the session. Every subsystem was affordable alone and
the arithmetic between them was the problem; no amount of re-reading was going to settle which one
dominated, and two separate confident guesses - the highlight gizmos, the router's four search
tiers - were wrong. It times whole subsystems (`recount`, `printer scan`, `autofly`, `highlight`)
and prints mean AND worst against a 50 ms tick budget.

**MEAN AND WORST, NEVER ONE OF THEM.** A recount costing two seconds every fortieth tick has a mean
of 50 ms and is the thing you can feel; the mean alone hides it among the ticks that did nothing,
and the worst alone cannot tell a one-off chunk load from a permanent cost. One `nanoTime` pair per
section per tick, no allocation, a fixed ring: a profiler left on overnight cannot grow.

    /cscan perf            what this mod costs the client thread, per subsystem
    /cscan perf reset      ...over the next window only

**Also found: `/cscan auto <name> 0` is a world capture EVERY TICK.** `everyMs = minutes * 60_000`
and the timer is satisfied on the tick it is set and every tick after it. Clamped to a minute
rather than refused - a typo should cost a slower scan, never the session.

### `Burial` - walled in on two sides, and nothing could see it

**EVERY WATCHDOG IN THIS MOD ASKS WHETHER THE LOOP IS TRAVELLING AND FAILING TO ARRIVE.**
`NOWHERE_MS`, the station stall, the thrash detector, the recovery ladder - all of them. A bot
standing exactly where it means to stand, breaking exactly the cells its dig list names, is not
travelling and is not failing: it is succeeding, one block at a time, into a pit of its own making.
The fault exists only in the GEOMETRY around the body, so that is what is measured.

Two halves, and neither is enough alone - a bot can be walled in by a trench it did not dig, and it
can sink through a floor with no walls at all:

- **`Digger.Verdict.UNDERFOOT`.** The floor you are standing on is not a cell to break. Tested
  against the BODY's own 0.6-wide footprint rather than `blockPosition()`, which is a rounded
  centre and says nothing about which blocks are carrying it. **POSITIONAL, so it is SKIPPED and
  never given up**: written off here, the loop could never come back and dig it from the side, and
  the design would carry a cell nobody may ever break.
- **`Burial.lift`.** Two of four sides walled - Jack's own threshold - and it rises. A side counts
  only when BOTH body cells are blocked, or every kerb in the park is a wall.

Three things it has to get right, each of which is a rule this project already paid for:

- **A ROOFED PLACE IS NOT A PIT, however walled it is.** A mine gallery, the undercroft, a tunnel
  the loop is meant to be inside: walled by design and roofed, so rising is grinding a ceiling -
  which `keepAirborne` has done. `canRise` is what makes the whole thing safe underground.
- **TWO SIDES IS ALSO A DOORWAY**, a corridor, and a trench between two spoil heaps. The geometry
  cannot tell those from a grave and TIME can, so it must hold for `HOLD_TICKS` (one second). A bot
  that lifts out of every doorway it steps into cannot build anywhere narrow.
- **IT ONLY EVER RISES, AND NEVER VIA THE JUMP KEY.** Which way is *out* is a search, and the
  recovery ladder owns searches; up is the one direction always right in a pit, and one course of
  it re-opens the sides, which ends it by itself. `jumpFromGround`, not the key - driving that key
  is a double tap inside seven ticks, which is the mistake that once revoked Jack's flight in
  mid-air.

It is checked in `Autopilot.tick` immediately after the fall rescue and ABOVE the destination
check, for the same reason the fall rescue is there: a bot digging itself in usually has nowhere it
is trying to go, which is precisely why nothing noticed.

`BurialTest` (8) is pure geometry with no client in it; 671 Java tests, 0 failures.

**Still open, and it needs a flight to settle.** The fixes above are reasoned from what each call
site costs multiplied by how often it runs, and the memoisation is certain to help - but WHICH
subsystem dominates has not been measured in game. Run `/cscan perf` while it is laggy; if
`recount` is still the top line, the next move is to stop building a fully-materialised todo list
for the whole design on every recount and give `Split` a global COUNT with a bounded cell list.

### The shopping list shouted loudest while achieving nothing (2026-09-06, chunkscan 0.8.7)

Jack: *"shopping list keeps getting spammed."*

`loadPlan` is cleared at the end of every recount that is not a fetch — *the list belongs to the
trip*, which is correct and is what stops a chest across the island re-sizing a list that was made
at the work. But the ANNOUNCEMENT was tied to the list being BUILT, and the list is rebuilt every
time it is missing. So whenever the loop wanted to fetch and could not — nothing indexed holds the
material, no room in the pack, every candidate chest still cooling off — it rebuilt an identical
list and said it again, **every two seconds, for as long as that stayed true.**

**IT WAS LOUDEST EXACTLY WHILE IT WAS ACHIEVING NOTHING**, which is this file's own rule about a
message on a two-second timer being a reason to turn the loop off, arrived at from a new direction:
the guard was on the wrong event. Building a list is not news; a trip changing is.

`saidLoadPlan` holds the last announced list and it is keyed on the **item SET, never the counts** —
the counts drift by a few every recount as the pack changes, so a signature carrying them is a
signature that always differs. What a trip IS, is what it is going to fetch. Reset when a new job
starts (`off`, a new design), never on the per-recount trip end, or the guard would clear itself on
exactly the tick it exists for.

**And the rest of the recount's messages were audited rather than assumed.** Every
`sendSystemMessage` inside `advance` was checked for a guard: three read as unguarded and all three
are one-shot state transitions that clear the condition as they fire (`topUp = false`, the
re-anchor, the design-complete hand-off). This was the only one that could repeat.

### ...and it was still spamming, because the list itself was never the same twice (chunkscan 0.8.9)

Jack, on 0.8.7: *"shopping list is getting constantly spammed and stopping all progress."* The
guard was right and it was guarding a thing that genuinely changed on every recount, and **the
same line that made it change is what stopped the progress**:

    if (!fetching) loadPlan = null;                      // the list belongs to the trip

**A TRIP IS NOT ONE RECOUNT.** Cleared on any phase that was not a FETCH, the list was thrown away
and remade every two seconds in exactly the states where the loop is oscillating — PACK_FULL, a
DEAD_END, every candidate chest still cooling off. A remade list is a DIFFERENT list, and the list
picks the chest: a new target every two seconds, a flight redirected before it arrives, and the
announcement again each time. One line, both halves of the report.

**AND THE CUT POINT OF A CELL BUDGET IS UNSTABLE BY CONSTRUCTION.** `loadPlan` filled to
`empty slots x 64` cells, ordered by course and then by distance to the anchor — and the anchor
drifts as cells go in while the budget shrinks as the pack fills, so **which materials fell either
side of the line moved on every recount.** The signature is the item SET, so it changed too. A
budget that reaches into forty materials is also the "stacks up with random resources" complaint
from two sessions ago: a trip for forty things finishes none of them.

Three changes, in that order of importance:

- **A trip is a handful of materials.** `Plan.MAX_MATERIALS` is 6 — enough that a course of
  masonry with its trim and its lighting is one journey. A material past the cap is SKIPPED rather
  than ending the walk, or the list would depend on the order the area happened to arrive in.
  Capped at MATERIALS the list is a decision rather than an accident, and it changes only when the
  WORK does: the same area at two different budgets is now the same list.
- **The list is kept until the trip is actually over** — `Hud.tripOver`: the pack holds it
  (`Plan.covered`), the anchor moved more than 24, the design changed, or it is five minutes old.
  Plus the healthy case, which is what the old line was reaching for: the phase came back BUILD
  with something to place, so the trip was declined.
- **And it is said at most once a minute** whatever else happens. A signature is a guard against
  repeating yourself; a clock is a guard against a future list finding a new way to differ.

675 Java tests, `chunkscan-0.8.9.jar` built, not flown.

## The autonomy audit (2026-09-06) — and the thing underneath all of it

Jack: *"audit carefully and identify how we improve this all functionally."* Four parallel read-only
audits — the loop's decisions, movement, placement and materials, the Python pipeline — plus a
measurement pass over the design that is actually being printed. Everything below was verified in
the code or against the artifact before it was written down; findings that could not be verified are
marked as such rather than listed.

### THE LOOP IS A LAST MILE WITH NO SUPPLY CHAIN

Measured against `Park Complete` (541,753 cells, 182 materials) and the live container index:

| | |
|---|---|
| materials the PARK-LOCAL chests can cover | **9 of 180** |
| blocks with no reachable source | **413,685 (76%)** |
| materials not indexed anywhere at all | 86, 69,281 blocks |
| worst single line | `moss_block`: **103,089 short** — and it has no recipe, because moss is a bone-meal FARM |
| the old island's chests | 180 containers, **~121,000 blocks away** — `Loop.FETCH_RADIUS` is 400 and `Nav.MAX_RANGE` is 512 |

**Every stall, every spam, every flight fix this month has been the last mile of a journey whose
goods were never made.** The mod can already `craft`, `smelt`, `buy`, `farm` and `take`; nothing
plans acquisition as part of a build, so the loop's honest answer to most of this design is a shrug.
The single highest-value thing that could be built is a PROVISIONING phase: given a design, resolve
what must be made, bought or farmed, drive those commands until a park-local work package is
covered, and only then start placing. Until then a "build the park" instruction is 76% unbuildable
and the loop cannot say so.

Two supporting facts, both measured:

- **A trip is sized in stacks, never in boxes.** `Work.loadCapacity` is `empty slots x 64`, so the
  biggest possible load is 2,304 blocks and the park needs **235 of them**. A shulker box holds
  1,728, the mod already takes boxes and already unpacks them — sizing a trip in boxes is ~9 trips
  instead of 235. Nothing does the arithmetic in boxes.
- **`prices.json` does not exist**, so `/cscan buy` and `cheapen --by-price` are inert: the shop has
  never been walked.

### The craft resolver plans 3,358 IRON PICKAXES

`python -m mcbuild craft "Park Complete"` proposes smelting 3,358 iron pickaxes into nuggets for 426
lanterns — **10,074 iron ingots where 379 would do**, on the island whose scarce metal is iron.

The cause is two faults compounding, and the first is a FIX FOR SOMETHING ELSE. `mark_reversible`
bars packing pairs from cost-minimisation because costing every leaf at 1 makes `raw_gold_block` a
cheaper source of raw gold than raw gold. True — and `iron_ingot -> 9 iron_nugget` is a packing pair
too, so the CORRECT and only sane route to a nugget is barred, leaving "smelt a tool" as the winner.
On top of that `raw_cost` returns **1.0 for `iron_nugget`, `iron_ingot` and `iron_pickaxe` alike**:
anything not derivable more cheaply is a leaf costing one, so a crafted tool is as cheap as an
ingot. A guard against arbitrage produced arbitrage.

### Python and Java disagree about what a block IS

Three separate drifts, all of them the repo's own one-source rule broken across the language
boundary, and all three now measured:

- **The item name.** `ActionRecipe.itemFor` maps `water -> water_bucket`, `oak_wall_sign ->
  oak_sign`, `water_cauldron -> cauldron`. Python has no such map, so `craft`, `analyze` and `shop`
  ask for items that cannot exist and report them as unobtainable: **7,965 cells**, 7,803 of them
  water.
- **The block state.** `work.INTENTIONAL` (Python) and `StateContract.INTENTIONAL` (Java) are the
  same list written twice and have drifted: Java additionally requires `waterlogged`, `powered`,
  `persistent` and `open`. Measured on the shipped composite: `persistent=true` 14,808,
  `powered=true` 1,184, **`open=true` 147**. The rails are already declined as commissioning, and a
  placed leaf IS persistent — but nothing in the mod opens a trapdoor, so **147 cells can never
  match, `todo` never empties, and `placementComplete()` is never true.** A design that cannot
  finish is a `follow all` that never moves on.
- **`analyze.clickable` vs `Printer.support`.** Two hand-written lists, drifted badly: Python said
  yes to every chest, barrel, furnace, hopper, door, trapdoor, fence gate, bed, note block, jukebox,
  cauldron, lectern, bell and flower pot — and to bare `torch`, which `endswith("_torch")` never
  caught. That is not a reporting nicety: `printable.closure` chains through it and
  `printable.stitch_model` WRITES the result into the shipped composite. **FIXED by porting
  `Printer.support` rather than paraphrasing it**, and the corrected rule immediately exposed
  diagonal breaks the loose one had hidden.

### Six defects fixed in this pass

- **THE SPOT COOLING-OFF WAS COMMENTED OUT.** `Hud.java:1249` had two statements on one line, so
  everything after the first `//` was a comment and `Loop.avoided` was never called — populated,
  cleared, never read. `abandonSpot` nulls `spotCentre`, so the next recount re-picked the SAME best
  cluster, flew at the same wall and stuck again: abandon, re-pick, abandon, every two seconds, until
  `THRASH_LIMIT` killed a design that had one awkward spot in it. The whole `AVOID_MS` machinery has
  never run.
- **The vicinity hold forbade its own printer.** The hold returns before `BuildJob.decide`, so the
  phase stayed whatever the last recount set — `PARKED` after a dead end or a look — and
  `AutomationControl.enter(PRINT)` refuses unless the phase is `BUILD`. The loop announced it was
  staying until the cells were in, placed nothing because it had forbidden itself, and blamed the
  world five seconds later.
- **A SUCCESSFUL look counted as a look FAILURE.** `Autopilot.arrivedAt` is true precisely when the
  flight REACHED the cell; two successful hops onto already-built ground therefore wrote the design
  off as finished. The failure is arriving and the chunk STILL not being loaded, which is what it
  tests now. And with autofly off `parked` was permanently false, so the look branch returned true
  every recount for ever — no placement, no fetch, no message, and no clock able to see it.
- **`Burial` was a regression I shipped in 0.8.6.** `Nav.standoff` prefers a spot with headroom, so
  `canRise` is true at EVERY station it picks; two walled sides is standing beside the wall you are
  building. Fired there it outranked arrival and steering: rise, sides open, fly back down, for ever.
  It is gated to the case it was written for — the digger working, or no destination at all — and a
  body walled in WITH somewhere to go is the recovery ladder's case, which already escalates from
  not-moving. Its step also set velocity directly, bypassing `Bounds.clamp` and `avoid`: the one
  movement path never tested against a block, on a server where contact ends flight. The caller owns
  the step now; `Burial` owns only the decision.
- **`park_place.py --ship` silently withdrew the mod's permission to build.** `Designs
  .requireAutonomousApproval` refuses any design whose `anchor_status` says preview/provisional/
  rebase and demands `automation_approved: true`. **No Python in this repo has ever written either
  key** — they were set by hand — and `save_pair` replaces a sidecar rather than merging, so the next
  ship would have reverted both and the mod would have refused the park with a message about a
  status string nobody set. A ship re-states geometry; it does not withdraw consent.
- **`/cscan auto <name> 0` is a world capture every tick.** Clamped to a minute.

### Found, verified, NOT fixed — these need a decision, not a patch

- **2,988 cells are in the design AND on the dig list.** Measured: 2,082 of them water, 2,933 at
  Y202, the ground plane. The mod has no way to express "break this, then place that" — `split` puts
  the cell in `todo` and `digLeft` returns the same cell as still standing, on the same tick, under
  the same radius. An unattended printer can place and re-break one block for ever. `park_place
  .complete()` honours the dig list for the ground and the railway but not module-against-module.
- **`work.json` is 21 MB that nothing reads.** `Work.cached` takes the litematic path whenever a
  `.litematic` exists, which is always; `loadWork` is a dead fallback. It is also written at only 2
  of 21 places a design is written — `Park Buildings.work.json` on disk is a day older than its own
  litematic. The structural answer is to make it a small MANIFEST (origin, digest, dig list, `after`,
  approval, the needs-a-hand set) emitted by `scan.save_pair`, and to ship the print ORDER that
  `printable.closure` already computes and throws away.
- **`overTop` is unbudgeted and unranged.** It runs before any tier deadline is consulted and is
  gated only on distance >= 4, so a cross-park hop walks thousands of heightmap lookups and ~20k
  `Nav.clear` samples before the first search starts — then every tier "fails" on a deadline that had
  already passed, and reports no route where the geometry was never examined.
- **A budget failure is indistinguishable from "no route", and two of them delete an 8-block cube of
  the park for the session.** `Ignored` has no expiry, and three unrelated give-up paths all strike
  the same key.
- **A moving destination resets the recovery ladder**, so in follow mode — where the target re-aims
  as cells are placed — `trouble` is zeroed before it reaches the first rung and the whole
  escalation is dead code.
- **`Work.room` assumes a 64 stack** for any item the pack is not already carrying, and the shared
  `dumpFree` slot budget is credited to EVERY item independently — so `PACK_FULL` is unreachable
  while one junk stack is held, and a withdrawal over-asks and then blacklists the chest that
  actually had the material for 60s.
- **`Work.tally` counts a double slab as one item and a door as two.** Small here (0 double slabs, 6
  door cells, 97 two-cell plants) but wrong in both directions.
